name: Magneton
smogon_description:
Magneton's niche lies in its access to Magnet Pull, which allows it to trap and revenge kill the omnipresent Scizor. It can also reliably trap and remove key Steel-types in Klefki and Empoleon, which can open the door for teammates like Latias, Mega Altaria, and Nihilego to more easily sweep. Outside of trapping Steel-types, Magneton has decent offensive presence thanks to its high Special Attack, decent dual STAB coverage, and access to STAB Volt Switch. It can also utilize its decent defensive typing to pivot in on passive attackers like Florges and Togekiss if need be. Unfortunately, Magneton's niche is often offset by its pitiful bulk, which mostly prevents it from taking advantage of its useful resistances or reliably coming into play. This can complicate its ability to trap Scizor due to its fear of directly switching in, often requiring that it accomplish its role with support from a pivoting teammate or through aggressive double switching. This also hampers its ability to check many Pokemon most other Steel-types can handle, such as Latias and Nihilego. Magneton's poor defensive capabilities are further compounded by its weaknesses to common Ground-, Fighting-, and Fire-type moves, which are often run as coverage by several Pokemon it could otherwise pressure, like Mega Aggron, Mega Altaria, and Togekiss. Its Speed is also extremely poor for an offensive Pokemon, leaving it outsped by the vast majority of the offensive metagame without a Choice Scarf and by Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl and Zeraora even with a Choice Scarf. These flaws often prevent Magneton from being able to reliably provide for its team outside of its role as a trapper, meaning it faces severe competition from other Electric-types with stronger defining characteristics and niches, like Rotom-H and Mega Manectric, and should usually never be run unless trapping Steel-types is desired, making it a very niche Pokemon.
Of the two Electric-type attacks Magneton runs, Thunderbolt is the most powerful, making it a useful option in situations in which Magneton wishes to wallbreak without pivoting out of play. It's also useful for reliably 2HKOing Empoleon and Klefki while pressuring bulky Water-types. Hidden Power Fire cleanly OHKOes Scizor, Magneton's primary target, while dealing respectable damage to Mega Steelix. It is important to note, however, that it deals less damage than Thunderbolt to any Steel-type other than the two mentioned. Flash Cannon deals decent damage to various Pokemon that may try switching in on an Electric-type attack, notably 2HKOing both Hippowdon and Latias after Stealth Rock damage. It also hits Florges and Sylveon super effectively. Volt Switch pivots Magneton out of play as it forces switches. It can also be useful for guaranteeing heavy chip damage on Mega Aggron without fear of its Earthquake.
Choice Specs puts considerable power behind Magneton's attacks, allowing it to 2HKO Empoleon and Klefki with Thunderbolt while OHKOing Scizor with Hidden Power Fire after Stealth Rock damage. Magnet Pull lets Magneton trap and remove Steel-types such as Empoleon, Scizor, Klefki, and Bronzong.
Magneton's most effective method of removing Steel-types like Scizor and Bronzong is through coming in on them on an aggressive double switch, as they will be cautious of staying in play very long in fear of getting trapped. This strategy is quite risky and prediction reliant, however. If Magneton is being run alongside a partner holding Eject Button, like Amoonguss or Alomomola, it should try utilizing them to freely come in on Scizor. Magneton's poor bulk prevents it from reliably coming in on many Pokemon, including those it traps, meaning its best opportunities to come into play are through the support of a pivot or after a teammate has fainted. However, Magneton's typing can allow it to come in on a few resisted weak attacks, like Florges's Moonblast and Amoonguss's Giga Drain, if need be. It can most easily come in on Klefki, which is unable to remotely dent Magneton due to usually only running Play Rough to deal damage. Steel-types that can tank at least one hit and punish Magneton, like Mega Aggron and Stakataka, should be hit with Volt Switch in order for Magneton to guarantee solid chip damage while preventing itself from being OHKOed or crippled. Due to this set's decent power, it can function as a formidable early- to mid-game wallbreaker. However, Magneton should only try doing this if trapping Steel-types isn't needed or if it's already accomplished its role. Volt Switch should be spammed the most out of Magneton's attacks due to its ability to deal decent damage, chip switch-ins, and generate momentum as Magneton forces switches. If a Ground-type is predicted to switch in on an expected Volt Switch, it is best for Magneton to try nabbing them with Flash Cannon, as the likes of Hippowdon, Gligar, and Krookodile can all be 2HKOed by the attack, though the former often requires some prior damage. Mega Steelix is an exception, however, as it doesn't take meaningful damage from Flash Cannon but is weak to Fire-type moves, meaning Magneton should use Hidden Power Fire to nail it on the switch if it expects Mega Steelix to come in.
Magneton fits well on offensive teams that appreciate a surefire way of removing Scizor. Dragon-types, such as Mega Altaria, Haxorus, and Latias, greatly appreciate Magneton's ability to remove or heavily weaken troublesome Steel-types for them, like Scizor and Mega Aggron. Other offensive Pokemon like Celebi, Mega Sharpedo, Togekiss, and Nihilego appreciate Magneton's ability to reliably remove or weaken Bronzong, Empoleon, Klefki, and Scizor. Pokemon that are particularly weak to Scizor due to its priority, such as Terrakion and Gengar, also appreciate Magneton as a teammate. Although its intended purpose isn't to pressure Water- and Fairy-types, Magneton can do this well with this set's breaking power, providing various sweepers, like Infernape, with easier opportunities to clean up. Magneton itself enjoys pivoting support from partners like Infernape, Scizor, Mega Beedrill, and Hydreigon due to its limited opportunities to safely switch in. It also appreciates Pokemon capable of taking on Ground-types reliably, like Tsareena, Primarina, and Togekiss. Electric-type checks such as Kyurem and Gligar are often solid teammates due to Magneton's inability to adequately damage the likes of Mega Manectric and Zeraora. Pokemon capable of breaking past specially defensive foes that Magneton can't muscle through, like Blissey and Alolan Muk, are also good partners, making Terrakion and Crawdaunt solid options. Pokemon with the ability Regenerator, like Amoonguss and Alomomola, can utilize an Eject Button to safely get Magneton in against an opposing Scizor, as it commonly finds itself using U-turn against them. Pokemon that can deal with Latias and Celebi are necessary, as Magneton is incapable of switching into them, so the likes of Mamoswine, Scizor, and Mimikyu make great partners.
Thunderbolt is Magneton's stronger Electric-type STAB attack, requiring much less chip damage for it to revenge kill Pokemon like Cobalion and Togekiss. It also OHKOes Moltres and Starmie. Hidden Power Fire's only use is to hit all variants of Scizor, Magneton's main target, for heavy damage, only failing to OHKO bulkier variants. Other than Scizor and Mega Steelix, all other Steel-types are hit harder by Thunderbolt. Flash Cannon can allow Magneton to revenge kill Pokemon like Terrakion, unboosted Mega Altaria, and Mamoswine. Volt Switch pivots Magneton out of play, allowing it to adequately chip Steel-types it can't OHKO while generating momentum.
Choice Scarf lets Magneton outpace Cobalion and revenge kill it after some chip damage. It also allows Magneton to surprise and more easily take on Pokemon like Mamoswine, Starmie, and Kyurem. Magnet Pull is essential in allowing Magneton to trap opposing Steel-types.
This set aims to reliably revenge kill Scizor with Hidden Power Fire, removing it from play. Since Magneton won't be able to directly switch in and opposing Scizor will be playing cautiously to avoid getting trapped, Magneton's best opportunities to come in on it are through double switches from Pokemon that often lure Scizor in, like Fairy- and Psychic-types. Magneton's frailty often means that its most reliable methods of coming in will be through a teammate's pivoting support or after a teammate has fainted. It can, however, come in on weak resisted hits from relatively passive Pokemon like Florges and Diancie. Magneton should take advantage of its enhanced Speed to function as a decent revenge killer, as it can outrun and KO several common fast offensive threats, like Gengar, Starmie, and Nihilego, after some chip damage. One of this set's main draws is its ability to more easily take on Cobalion. Thus, Magneton should try finding an opportunity to come in on Cobalion, chip it with Volt Switch if it isn't in range of Thunderbolt, and revenge kill it with Thunderbolt when it's weakened enough. Volt Switch should be used to generate momentum on forced switches after Magneton has accomplished trapping its designated targets. However, due to this set's lower damage output, Magneton must look out for letting defensive Ground-types like Gligar and Hippowdon in for free. Despite the increased Speed Choice Scarf provides, Magneton will still not be able to outrun especially fast Pokemon such as Mega Aerodactyl, Zeraora, Mega Beedrill, and Mega Manectric. It is also slower than most opposing Choice Scarf users, like Hydreigon and Krookodile. Due to this, it is not advised to stay in on those threats.
Offensive teams that appreciate the removal of Steel-types, particularly Scizor, value Magneton for its ability to do this while functioning as an adequate revenge killer if need be. Dragon-types like Latias and Mega Altaria particularly appreciate Magneton's support, making them excellent partners. Pokemon that appreciate Fairy-type checks on their team, like Hydreigon, also pair well with Magneton. Pokemon with Regenerator, like Alomomola and Amoonguss, can use Eject Button to allow Magneton a free opportunity to switch in against Scizor, making its role much easier to accomplish. Magneton itself appreciates Ground-type checks, like Mega Blastoise, Togekiss, and Celebi, as well as Pokemon capable of answering Electric-types, such as Krookodile, Gligar, and Mega Altaria. It also values support from pivots capable of safely bringing it into play, like Infernape, Scizor, and Tsareena. Powerful wallbreakers are also appreciated by Magneton for their ability to weaken Pokemon into range of its attacks due to this set's middling power. This makes Nidoking and Mamoswine worthy teammates. Checks to faster threats like Mega Aerodactyl, Zeraora, and Mega Manectric are necessary, so Pokemon like Hippowdon, Mega Altaria, Nidoqueen, and Rhyperior make great partners. Offensive Psychic- and Dragon-types like Latias and Celebi give Magneton a hard time, as it struggles to break past and check them, therefore partners capable of checking them such as Scizor, Blissey, and Mega Aerodactyl are essential. Lastly, Magneton appreciates entry hazard support on its team, particularly for allowing it to more easily KO bulky Scizor sets with Hidden Power Fire, making Nihilego and Gligar worthwhile teammates.
A set utilizing Electrium Z and Substitute can be used to better trap and remove bulkier Steel-types such as Mega Aggron while still being strong enough to remove Scizor. However, this comes at the cost of taking up the Z-Move from a partner that would benefit from it better as well as leaving Magneton completely walled by Mega Steelix.
Faster Pokemon: Magneton's poor bulk allows faster threats such as Terrakion, Krookodile, and Mega Sharpedo to heavily threaten it with powerful STAB moves. Even its Choice Scarf set can be outpaced and threatened by Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Manectric, and Zeraora, as well as faster Choice Scarf users like Infernape, Krookodile, and Hydreigon.
Electric-types: Electric-types resist Magneton's STAB combination, and all have various ways of punishing it. Zeraora is immune to Thunderbolt and Volt Switch by virtue of its access to Volt Absorb, and it can either punish Magneton for setup turns or KO it with Close Combat. Mega Manectric can utilize its base forme ability in Lightning Rod to gain a Special Attack boost upon coming in on Magneton's Electric-type attacks while forcing it out with Overheat. Rotom-H resists any attack Magneton can throw at it while threatening to KO it with Overheat.
Ground-types: The likes of Hippowdon, Krookodile, Nidoking, and Gligar can all take a hit and OHKO Magneton with super effective STAB attacks. While Mamoswine fears coming in on Flash Cannon, it too can force Magneton out with its 4x super effective Earthquake. Mega Steelix is particularly troublesome, as it is only hit hard by the rather punishable Choice Specs-boosted Hidden Power Fire and can KO Magneton with Earthquake, set up Stealth Rock on it, or set up with Curse. Swampert is also a particularly effective check because it resists any common attack Magneton can throw at it.
Specially Bulky Pokemon: Specially bulky Pokemon often have easy ways of taking Magneton on. Blissey doesn't fear any of its attacks and can wear it down with Seismic Toss or perform one of its many potential utility roles. While Alolan Muk doesn't love taking repeated Volt Switches, it can threaten to trap Magneton with Pursuit or cripple it with Knock Off. Snorlax can also repeatedly sponge hits from Magneton while using it to set up with Curse or outright KOing it with Earthquake.

name: Farfetch'd
smogon_description:
Farfetch'd is unsurprisingly an awful choice because its stats are pitiful and it's hopelessly outclassed by many other Flying-types in the tier. While it has some eye-catching quirks like First Impression, it often flops compared to other options for wallbreakers or priority users due to its unspectacular Speed tier and nearly complete lack of defensive utility making it easy to revenge kill. Dodrio and Scyther in particular sport Swords Dance as well and have much better Speed tiers. Farfetch'd also struggles to put a dent in Steel-types and Oricorio-E, despite its decent movepool otherwise.
Farfetch'd can attempt to offensively check certain threats like Absol and Jynx, and can annoy typical Flying-type checks such as Regirock and Aurorus with its coverage. However, outside of First Impression, Farfetch'd remains completely outclassed by better physical Flying- and Normal-types like Scyther, Dodrio, and Kangaskhan.

name: Galarian Farfetch'd
smogon_description:
Final Gambit gives Galarian Farfetch'd a unique niche on teams with Mienfoo. If it can't clean late-game with its powerful STAB Close Combat, good coverage, and Choice Scarf, Final Gambit lets it remove a check for another teammate to sweep. Final Gambit, with this EV spread, OHKOes Mareanie after Stealth Rock, Koffing, and Mienfoo, three potential checks to Galarian Farfetch'd; however, it should be used carefully to avoid a disadvantageous trade. Natu is a very effective team partner for Galarian Farfetch’d, able to block entry hazards with Magic Bounce to allow a full strength Final Gambit. Natu, and other Pokemon checked by Steel-types like Abra, Staryu, and Porygon, all appreciate Galarian Farfetch’d pressuring Steel-types. They can pressure Poison-types in return.
When equipped with a Life Orb, Galarian Farfetch'd is an incredibly strong wallbreaker that can defeat common Fighting-type switch-ins due to its sheer power. Knock Off weakens switch-ins such as Koffing and Mareanie, leaving them vulnerable to be 2HKOed by Close Combat after slight chip damage. Brave Bird hits Fighting-types, Larvesta, and Foongus. Quick Attack can finish off low health, faster Pokemon such as Focus Sash Abra brought down to 1 HP, as well as low health Diglett, and Carvanha. Galarian Farfetch'd can form a Fighting spam core with Mienfoo or Timburr to help break down opposing Fighting-type checks, such as Koffing. Pivots such as Larvesta and Trace Porygon can use U-turn or Teleport, respectively, to get Galarian Farfetch'd onto the field to fire off its powerful attacks, as well as helping with its lack of defensive utility.

name: Doduo
smogon_description:
Doduo's excellent Attack stat, powerful STAB moves, and good coverage options make it one of the best physical attackers in the LC metagame. It typically takes on the role of a powerful wallbreaker, using its very good Speed stat and coverage options to wear down opposing teams or to end games against slower teams. It is helped in its wallbreaking by its coverage options, which make it impossible to safely switch into. Doduo can also flip its wallbreaking set on its head and run a Choice Scarf set, which outspeeds most of the Pokemon that typically revenge kill it and can reliably clean up weakened teams late-game. However, Doduo suffers from poor defensive stats that leave it vulnerable to revenge killing and priority attacks. Furthermore, its most powerful and spammable move, Brave Bird, has significant recoil damage, which, coupled with its Stealth Rock weakness, means it tends to get worn down very fast.
Brave Bird is an incredibly powerful STAB attack that does significant damage to anything that doesn't resist it, though at the cost of dealing significant recoil damage to Doduo. Knock Off can be used to remove the items of Pokemon that switch into Doduo, softening them up for Doduo or its teammates to better deal with them. Jump Kick hits Rock- and Steel-type Pokemon for super effective damage, making it risky for these Pokemon to switch into a predicted Brave Bird. Quick Attack gives Doduo a priority move that hits fairly hard thanks to its high Attack. Return is an alternative that gives Doduo another powerful STAB move that hits Pokemon that resist Brave Bird and don't mind Jump Kick, such as Chinchou, without causing recoil damage, but most Pokemon are hit plenty hard by Doduo's first three moves. Substitute is a possibility as well, which lets Doduo activate Berry Juice when necessary and play around Pawniard's Sucker Punch.
The given EV spread maximizes Doduo's Attack, to allow it to hit as hard as possible, and its Speed, to allow it to outspeed a majority of the metagame while breaking it down. With a Jolly nature, Doduo hits 18 Speed, allowing it to become even harder to switch into and reliably outspeed the likes of Cottonee, Snivy, and Chinchou. Berry Juice is useful to allow Doduo to take weak priority attacks or switch into Stealth Rock more times during a match, making it less prone to getting worn down. Early Bird is the preferred ability, as both of Doduo's other abilities are practically useless competitively.
Doduo should be brought in either by a slow pivot or after a Pokemon faints, as it doesn't have the bulk to take even most resisted hits reliably. After it comes in, Doduo can spam its powerful attacks. Knock Off is a good choice early-game to wear down Doduo's checks and counters. After Pokemon that resist Flying have been worn down or picked off with Jump Kick, Doduo can spam Brave Bird to clean up opposing teams. Scouting for opposing Choice Scarf users is helpful so Doduo isn't unexpectedly outsped while attempting to attack.
Slow pivots allow Doduo to enter the match safely. Mienfoo does this well, as it can also beat the Rock- and Steel-types that threaten Doduo while wearing down teams with Knock Off, as does Chinchou, which checks the Electric-type Pokemon that resist Brave Bird. Pokemon such as Onix, Omanyte, and Archen synergize with Doduo fairly well and can set up entry hazards that wear down opposing teams and make Doduo even more difficult to switch into. Entry hazard control is also appreciated; Staryu and Drilbur can spin away Stealth Rock that wears Doduo down. Offensive Pokemon that share checks and counters with Doduo can wear down said Pokemon. Other Flying-types work especially well, including Vullaby and Rufflet. Diglett also makes a very good partner to Doduo, being able to trap and remove Rock-, Steel-, and Electric-type Pokemon that aim to check it. Lastly, Healing Wish and Z-Memento users, such as Cottonee, make good partners for Doduo, allowing it to wear down its own checks and counters and then healing it to sweep late in the game.
Brave Bird is Doduo's most powerful and spammable move, dealing enormous damage to anything that doesn't resist it. Knock Off removes defensive items, such as Eviolite and Berry Juice, from switch-ins to Doduo, allowing Doduo or its teammates to beat them more easily late in the match. Jump Kick hits the Steel- and Rock-types that resist Brave Bird for super effective damage and makes Doduo very hard to switch into. Return is another powerful STAB move that doesn't inflict recoil damage on Doduo while still hitting what doesn't resist it for good damage. Quick Attack is an alternative that lets Doduo act as an emergency revenge killer against weakened faster Pokemon or weakened Pokemon with priority.
The given EV spread maximizes Doduo's Attack and Speed stats so it can clean as well as possible. With a Jolly nature and a Choice Scarf, Doduo hits 27 Speed, tying with Choice Scarf Gastly and outspeeding Choice Scarf users such as Chinchou and Mienfoo as well as boosted Pokemon such as Dragon Dance Scraggy and most Shell Smash Omanyte and Shellder. Choice Scarf Doduo also outspeeds Adamant Alolan Sandshrew in hail and Modest Bellsprout in sun, so it can check weather teams if necessary. An Adamant nature can be run to increase Doduo's attacking power, but it will Speed tie with some of the aforementioned threats and lose to the weather sweepers. Early Bird is used because Doduo's other two abilities are more or less competitively useless.
Use this set as a revenge killer or a late-game cleaner. Avoid switching Doduo into attacks, as it has poor bulk and already is worn down quickly due to its reliance on Brave Bird to clean opposing teams. Once it is in, Doduo can spam its powerful Brave Bird, or, if Rock-type checks have yet to be weakened, lure them in and KO or weaken them with Knock Off or Jump Kick. If Doduo is attempting to clean late-game, be wary of Brave Bird recoil damage, and lock Doduo into Return if possible.
Entry hazards are extremely helpful to wear down Pokemon so Doduo can take them out. Teammates such as Onix, Omanyte, and Dwebble can set Stealth Rock effectively and have good synergy with Doduo. This Doduo set can't wear down its own checks and counters very well due to its inability to switch moves, so Pokemon that can wear these checks and counters down for it make good partners. Meowth, Vullaby, and Rufflet all bring in common checks to Doduo and can wear them down for Doduo to sweep later in a game. Slow pivots allow Doduo to enter the match safely. Mienfoo does this well, as it can also beat the Rock- and Steel-types that threaten Doduo while wearing down teams with Knock Off, as does Chinchou, which checks the Electric-type Pokemon that resist Brave Bird. Finally, Diglett makes a good partner to Doduo, able to trap and remove Rock-, Steel-, and Electric-type Pokemon that aim to check it.
Life Orb makes Doduo one of the hardest-hitting attackers in the metagame, enhancing its wallbreaking capability, but this often lets it attack only two or three times over the course of a game before KOing itself with recoil. Double-Edge is an option for a more powerful Normal-type STAB move, but it comes with high recoil damage to Doduo. Various Hidden Powers, including Hidden Power Grass, can be run to surprise various checks to Doduo that aren't KOed by a coverage move, such as Tirtouga. A Focus Sash set with Flail or Endeavor and Quick Attack is possible, but it requires substantial support to use. Swords Dance can be used to bring Doduo's Attack to insane levels, but due to its frailty, Doduo will rarely be able to get the move off safely. Agility can be used to boost Doduo's Speed, but, similarly to Swords Dance, Doduo has trouble finding opportunities to use it. Drill Peck can be used as a Flying-type STAB move with no recoil, but it comes at the cost of substantial power. Thrash is a more powerful Normal-type STAB move, but it locks Doduo into it, which can give the Pokemon that resist it free setup turns. Steel Wing is a potential coverage move for Archen, but it forces Doduo to forgo more generally useful coverage. Roost is a possibility to recover Doduo's HP, but Doduo will usually not get this opportunity because it is so frail. Finally, Facade is an option as an extremely powerful Normal-type STAB move for when Doduo is inflicted with a status condition, but most Pokemon that inflict status conditions will outright KO Doduo anyway.
Revenge Killers: As Doduo is nearly impossible to switch into safely, the best way to take it out is offensively. Choice Scarf users such as Magnemite, Chinchou, and Pawniard easily outspeed and KO non-Choice Scarf Doduo, as do naturally fast Pokemon such as Elekid and Abra. The Choice Scarf variant is more susceptible to priority, such as Pawniard's Sucker Punch, which will wear it down rapidly.
Rock-types: Rock-types, especially those with high Defense, make decent Doduo checks, though they have to be wary of Jump Kick. Weak Armor users such as Dwebble and Omanyte can take an attack while gaining a Speed boost and take out Doduo or set up Stealth Rock. Onix and Tirtouga both can survive a Jump Kick and KO in return, and defensive Archen deserves a special mention as one of the few Pokemon that are not 2HKOed by any Doduo variant from full health.
Electric-types: Electric-type Pokemon can make good checks to Doduo. Chinchou and Magnemite can take a hit and KO back or outspeed non-Choice Scarf Doduo with Choice Scarves of their own and revenge kill it. Elekid can outspeed non-Choice Scarf Doduo and take it out, although it takes substantial damage from Quick Attack, and Choice Scarf variants of Elekid are among the only Pokemon that outspeed and take out Choice Scarf Doduo.

name: Dodrio
smogon_description:
Dodrio's fantastic offensive stats, near-unresisted coverage, and access to Swords Dance solidify it as a top offensive threat in PU that's able to blitz through Pokemon found on offensive and defensive teams alike. It can run a variety of sets that each offer immense amounts of offensive pressure: Swords Dance and Choice Band sets excel at wallbreaking, whereas Choice Scarf sets boast a near-unrivaled Speed tier. Since all of Dodrio's sets fit on offensive teams, deciphering what set it's running from Team Preview is nearly impossible, giving Dodrio the upper hand in many situations. However, Dodrio's lackluster bulk and weakness to Stealth Rock limit what it can safely switch into or use Swords Dance on, and it is easily worn down by Brave Bird's high recoil. Dodrio's matchups are also highly set dependent, as wallbreaking sets are prone to being revenge killed, while Choice Scarf lacks the power to break through bulky walls like Regirock and Mudsdale.
Jump Kick gives Dodrio a way to threaten Steel- and Rock-types like Aggron and Kabutops, while notably allowing Dodrio to revenge kill Alolan Sandslash under hail. Knock Off provides Dodrio with unresisted coverage and can be used to weaken item-dependent Pokemon such as Mudsdale and Type: Null. Pursuit enables Dodrio to trap weakened offensive foes such as Alolan Raichu and Haunter, further solidifying this set's ability to revenge kill.
Choice Scarf grants Dodrio the ability to outspeed every other relevant Choice Scarf user. Choice Scarf Dodrio can also outspeed weather-reliant Pokemon such as Victreebel, Alolan Sandslash, and Ludicolo in addition to setup sweepers like +2 Omastar and Combusken.
Use Pursuit in order to trap weakened threats or Pokemon weak to Pursuit such as Oricorio-G and Haunter. This works out especially well if one decides to not reveal Choice Scarf until mid or late-game when Dodrio's checks are weakened, as this allows Dodrio to get the jump on foes like Alolan Raichu, Floatzel, and opposing Choice Scarf users like Scyther and Primeape. Knock Off can be used to weaken defensive checks early-game; however, avoid reckless use of such moves, as Pokemon like Aggron can switch into these moves easily. Prediction plays an important role when using this set, as Dodrio is incredibly frail and will not be able to do much to targets if it isn't locked into the best move. Late-game, Dodrio can liberally spam its STAB moves for optimal damage output once Rock- and Steel-type checks such as Omastar and Aggron are removed.
Fighting-types such as Gurdurr and Hitmonchan act as solid answers to Steel- and Rock-types like Aggron and Aurorus, and their removal allows Dodrio to use its STAB moves far more freely. Dodrio greatly appreciates specially offensive wallbreakers such as Aurorus, Drampa, and Jellicent to punch holes through physically defensive walls like Regirock, Mudsdale, and Carbink. Entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale, Regirock, and Qwilfish are pivotal to Choice Scarf Dodrio's role as a revenge killer, as they're able to wear down the opposing team to help Dodrio secure KOs. These examples are also able to cripple the opposing team with moves like Toxic and Scald. Since Dodrio will be coming in and out to pick off weakened threats, entry hazard removal from the likes of Skuntank and Alolan Sandslash is important so as to not let Dodrio be worn down. Lurantis can breeze past checks to Dodrio such as Sableye, Mudsdale, and Carracosta, while Silvally-Dragon can chip at physical walls with a powerful Draco Meteor and provide momentum for Dodrio through Parting Shot.
Jump Kick enables Dodrio to hit Rock- and Steel-types that resist its other moves such as Regirock, Aggron, and Aurorus. Return is a safe STAB option with no recoil; this is also Dodrio's strongest move against Electric-types like Oricorio-E and Lanturn. Quick Attack gives Dodrio a form of priority and does a solid amount to would-be revenge killers like Choice Scarf Primeape and Jynx, OHKOing the latter at +2.
Flyinium Z turns Brave Bird into Supersonic Skystrike, negating Brave Bird's hefty recoil and enabling Dodrio to OHKO targets such as Mudsdale and Ferroseed at +2 and Pokemon like Skuntank and Golurk without any boosts. Fightinium Z converts Jump Kick into All-Out Pummeling, allowing Dodrio to whistle past checks like Regirock and Carracosta, OHKOing both of them at +2 after Stealth Rock damage. This is also the item of choice when using Quick Attack over Return as to maximize damage against Electric-types such as Eelektross and Lanturn.
Dodrio should mainly be brought in through slow pivots or double switches to minimize chances of Dodrio getting chipped and generate good matchups. Dodrio can also switch into Ghost- and Ground-type attacks thanks to its immunities, though this is a risky endeavor due to its lousy defenses. Setting up with Swords Dance safely can be achieved against Pokemon that are forced out like Tangela and Lurantis, passive walls like Audino and Clefairy, and Choice-locked Pokemon like Jellicent. Avoid late-game setup if Dodrio lacks Quick Attack for faster revenge killers or if Pokemon that resist or are immune to Quick Attack such as Lycanroc and Choice Scarf Haunter are still around. Swords Dance doesn't necessarily have to be used in order for Dodrio to wallbreak; Dodrio's respective Z-Move can be thrown right off the bat to ensure that Pokemon like Simisear and Aggron drop. This is also effective at punishing Pokemon that may stay in predicting a Swords Dance. Outside of Swords Dance, Dodrio can be used as a revenge killer against slower Pokemon such as Scyther and unboosted Omastar. Dodrio's revenge killing capabilities are further bolstered against bulkier foes like Articuno and Stoutland through the use of Z-Crystals.
Bulky pivots such as Lanturn and Alolan Persian are able to bring Dodrio in as safely as possible and lure in Pokemon such as Roselia and Poliwrath for Dodrio to take advantage of. Lanturn and Alolan Persian are also solid switch-ins to moves such as Swanna’s Scald and Lycanroc's Stone Edge, respectively. Fighting-types such as Primeape and Gurdurr have amazing offensive synergy with Dodrio, as they can pressure Rock- and Ice-types such as Lycanroc and Abomasnow, while Dodrio can dispatch Pokemon like Tangela and Scyther in return. Hitmonchan can also remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin and switch into Pokemon such as Aurorus. Mudsdale, Torterra, and other Pokemon that are able to switch in on Rock-types can stomach hits from the likes of Lycanroc, which may attempt to revenge kill Dodrio. Entry hazard removal from the likes of Alolan Sandslash and Cryogonal keep Stealth Rock off of Dodrio's side, keeping it healthy and giving it more chances to set up or attack. Sponges to attacks such as Tangela, Mudsdale, and Metang are able to switch into Choice Scarf users that can revenge kill Dodrio like Kabutops, Primeape, and Jynx. Additional team support can be used to give Dodrio as many setup opportunities as possible. Jellicent and Sableye can cripple physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp, allowing Dodrio to set on weakened Pokemon like Scyther and Type: Null. Skuntank's Memento reduces the amount of damage Dodrio takes and provides momentum.
Knock Off gives Dodrio the ability to chip at and weaken switch-ins like Regirock and Metang by removing their items. Pursuit allows Dodrio to trap slower, weakened foes like Oricorio-G and offensive Jellicent. With a Choice Band, Dodrio is notably able to do around 70% to bulky Oricorio-G, securing an OHKO after Stealth Rock and slight residual damage. Quick Attack picks off weakened Pokemon that can otherwise outspeed Dodrio such as Choice Scarf Swanna and Primeape.
Choice Band allows Dodrio to immediately wallbreak, 2HKOing Pokemon like Ferroseed and OHKOing the likes of Golurk and Aggron right off the bat.
Given how most players maneuver around Dodrio's other sets, Choice Band's increase in power can be utilized to grab KOs on bulky Pokemon such as Stoutland and Gurdurr far more easily, as they may stay in fearing the possibility of Swords Dance. Pursuit should be used on predicted switches; for instance, Dodrio can OHKO Pokemon like Haunter and offensive Oricorio-G courtesy of Choice Band. If necessary, Dodrio can occasionally switch into moves like Golurk's Earthquake and Oricorio-G's Revelation Dance, but you must exercise caution when doing so because of Dodrio's poor bulk. Brave Bird's recoil can be put to use late-game by allowing Dodrio to KO itself, creating momentum for its team.
Pivots such as Lanturn and Alolan Persian can generate momentum for Dodrio and are able to bait in Pokemon such as Lurantis and Gurdurr. Choice Band Dodrio can form an offensive core with specially offensive wallbreakers such as Drampa, Jellicent, and Rotom-F, as these Pokemon target physically defensive walls like Regirock and Sableye, while Dodrio can break through Pokemon like Audino, Lurantis, and Hitmonchan in return. Entry hazard removal from the likes of Skuntank and Alolan Sandslash keeps Stealth Rock off the field, increasing the number of times Dodrio can switch in. Fighting-types like Gurdurr and Hitmonchan are able to dispatch Steel- and Rock-types early on, allowing Dodrio to use its STAB moves more frequently. Hitmonchan can also remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin. Pivots like Lanturn and Silvally-Dragon bring Dodrio in as safely as possible and can lure in Pokemon such as Lurantis and Clefairy. These two Pokemon can also weaken bulky walls like Regirock and Mudsdale. Late-game sweepers such as Lycanroc and Combusken greatly appreciate Dodrio's wallbreaking and the removal or weakening of Pokemon like Mudsdale and Lanturn.
Taunt + Roost can be used to give Dodrio the functionality of a stallbreaker, but such a set falls flat due to its shortage of attacking options. Moreover, this competes heavily with other stallbreakers such as Oricorio-E due to its superior defensive capabilities. Life Orb gives Dodrio freedom to switch between its moves and is not one-time use like Z-Crystals are, but Dodrio already struggles with being worn down from Stealth Rock damage and Brave Bird recoil.
Rock-types: Rock-types such as Regirock and Carracosta possess enough physical bulk to can switch into Dodrio lacking Fightinium Z and threaten it with their STAB moves. Regirock in particular has the most consistency when it comes to checking all of Dodrio's sets; it can easily switch into Choice-locked variants of Dodrio and OHKO it with Stone Edge, and it can viably run Chople Berry or Protect to sponge an All-Out Pummeling. Lycanroc and Choice Scarf Kabutops outspeed Dodrio lacking a Choice Scarf, and the former can use Dodrio as setup fodder if it's Choice-locked into Pursuit or Quick Attack. All of these Pokemon must be wary of taking a boosted All-Out Pummeling, however.
Set-dependent Switch-ins: Physically defensive walls such as Mudsdale and Sableye are able to switch into Dodrio lacking Flyinium Z and take very little from Choice Scarf Dodrio. They can then proceed to stall it out or cripple it with a burn, respectively. These Pokemon must be cautious of directly switching into Choice Band Dodrio, however. Oricorio-E, Aggron, and Aurorus can come in on Choice-locked Dodrio depending on what it's locked into and threaten it with their respective super effective moves.
Revenge Killers and Priority: Choice Scarf users such as Primeape and Swanna outspeed variants of Dodrio lacking Choice Scarf and obliterate it with their moves. Floatzel and Alolan Persian are naturally faster than Dodrio and can do serious damage to it with Ice Beam and Foul Play or Thunderbolt, respectively. Alolan Persian can also comfortably take Quick Attack thanks to Fur Coat. All variants of Dodrio are outsped by priority moves such as Kangaskhan's Fake Out and Abomasnow's Ice Shard, both of which do serious damage to it. Additionally, without Quick Attack, Dodrio has little to no way of playing around Sucker Punch users like Skuntank and Absol.
Residual Damage: Dodrio gets worn very easily by Brave Bird and has a weakness to Stealth Rock, which limits how many times it can come in or set up.

name: Seel
smogon_description:
Above-average defenses and access to some interesting support moves in Whirlpool and Perish Song allow Seel to carve out a niche role as the bulkiest Perish trapper, theoretically allowing it to take on a huge number of Pokemon in LC. The downsides are the strategy is one-dimensional and can be easy to play around once revealed, costing the user momentum. Other supporting Water-types such as Mareanie and Frillish are generally better choices, since they can compress multiple roles and fit better in the current metagame.
Perish trapping is a strategy good for removing a foe from the opposing team. Seel's above-average defenses give it ample room to pull of a successful trap and stall out damage. The drawback to this is once your opponent becomes aware of the strategy, it can be easy to play around with moves such as U-turn and Volt Switch or even with ample prediction, causing the momentum to go towards the opponent rather the user. Because of these limiting factors, it is a good rule of thumb to bring another utility Water-Type like Frillish or Mareanie. Regardless, if you're set on using Seel, Perish trapping is the way to go.

name: Dewgong
smogon_description:
Dewgong is completely outclassed as a bulky Water-type by Pokemon like Lanturn and Jellicent due to their better typing and lack of Stealth Rock weakness. Jellicent also has reliable recovery, and both have more valuable utility options such as Volt Absorb and Heal Bell for Lanturn, as well as Taunt and Will-O-Wisp for Jellicent. Dewgong's awful defensive typing also makes it extremely passive, so it can't even utilize its niche to the fullest extent; While it can be used on stall as a Perish trapper, Pyukumuku has a more valuable role on stall as a trapper with Block that can wear down opposing Pokemon with Toxic, punish setup sweepers with Unaware, and use reliable recovery in Recover.
The main goal of this set is to trap passive and defensive Pokemon and stall them out with Rest until they inevitably fall to Perish Song. This seems good on paper, but in actual play, this niche isn't important enough to separate Dewgong from Pyukumuku, which fills almost the same role as Dewgong but does a better job of it due to its massive defensive stats, better typing in pure Water, and lack of Stealth Rock weakness. Recover is also far more consistent as a form of recovery. This set is also extremely vulnerable to Pokemon that carry Taunt, which completely shut Dewgong down and render it useless.

name: Grimer
smogon_description:
Even though Grimer's Poison typing and Sticky Hold ability let it switch in on Fighting-types, as it resists their STAB attacks and does not risk losing its item, Trubbish does the same thing but better because of its higher Speed, access to entry hazards in Spikes, and repeated Berry Juice recovery with Recycle. Other bulky Poison-types like Foongus and Mareanie use their secondary typings to not completely fall flat to Diglett and to pivot effectively with Regenerator, respectively. Lastly, Alolan Grimer completely overshadows Grimer as a bulky Poison-type because of its Poison / Dark typing, granting only one weakness and having exclusive access to moves like Knock Off and Pursuit to effectively trap Abra and Gastly.
Grimer should switch in on Fighting-types, as it resists their STAB attacks and won't lose its item to Knock Off due to Sticky Hold, and then try hit hard with Gunk Shot or use its other moves when predicting certain Pokemon switching in. However, Grimer's low Speed and weaknesses to common types leave it vulnerable to being trapped by Diglett, making it hard to function. This leaves Grimer outclassed by Trubbish, as its greater Speed lets it perform Grimer's job more effectively, and it can set up Spikes or keep restoring its HP repeatedly with Recycle and Berry Juice.

name: Alolan Grimer
smogon_description:
Alolan Grimer boasts a solid Poison / Dark typing, which grants it a sole weakness to Ground. Its amazing typing is coupled with solid 80 / 50 / 50 bulk that is further boosted by Eviolite. It also has access to Poison Touch, which adds to its many contact moves the extra chance of poisoning. Alolan Grimer acts as a wonderful Pursuit trapper with a better typing than Pawniard and better bulk than Stunky; on top of this, it has a good STAB combination and access to coverage moves like Fire Punch for Steel-types. However, it is quite slow, meaning that it almost always has to take a hit before moving. It's also vulnerable to entry hazards and burns, and the lack of Berry Juice and reliable recovery limits its longevity.
With Pursuit, Alolan Grimer can trap threats such as Abra and Gastly while also trapping weakened foes such as Pumpkaboo-XL and Slowpoke. Knock Off is a powerful Dark-type STAB move with the bonus effect of removing items. Both of these moves also come with a 30% chance of poisoning foes thanks to Poison Touch. Poison Jab is the preferred move in the third moveslot because it has perfect accuracy, hits decently hard, and boasts an increased 51% chance of poisoning. On the other hand, Gunk Shot trades these for more power, notably OHKOing Spritzee after Stealth Rock damage most of the time. For the last moveslot, Shadow Sneak can be used to pick off weakened targets and to bypass Alolan Grimer's terrible Speed. Alternatively, Fire Punch hits the Steel-types that check Alolan Grimer, with a good chance to OHKO Ferroseed after one layer of Spikes and a guaranteed 2HKO on non-Eviolite Magnemite and Pawniard.
Maximum Attack investment is required to make Alolan Grimer hit as hard as possible. The leftover EVs are dumped into its defensive stats because it doesn't need Speed at all; they guarantee that Alolan Grimer is never 2HKOed by Life Orb Abra's Dazzling Gleam and, for Eviolite variants, never OHKOed by Jolly Focus Sash Diglett's Earthquake. Eviolite is the prime item of choice because it boosts Alolan Grimer's defenses to let it take hits better. Berry Juice, on the other hand, lengthens its lifespan, since it lacks any form of recovery. An alternative EV spread of 36 HP / 196 Atk / 36 Def / 196 SpD lets Alolan Grimer check Abra and Gastly more reliably but sacrifices some needed physical bulk, while a spread of 36 HP / 36 Atk / 196 Def / 196 SpD grants better mixed bulk to avoid most OHKOs but at the cost of significant offensive presence.
Alolan Grimer should spam Knock Off most of the time because it is a powerful STAB move with great utility and a good chance of poisoning; it should use Knock Off even if a Fairy-type such as Snubbull is switching in because removing its item helps with punishing it with Poison Jab or Gunk Shot later. Knock Off is also a good source of chip damage, increasing the chances to OHKO foes with Poison Jab. Pursuit severely dents fleeing foes, and the added bonus of possibly poisoning them is very useful because it deals some chip damage. Alolan Grimer should be sent in on Pokemon it can Pursuit trap, such as Abra and Gastly, because it can survive most hits and KO them back. Alolan Grimer is able to survive most powerful hits thanks to its typing and its bulk; however, keep in mind that it lacks a solid form of recovery besides Berry Juice. Finally, be wary of Volt Switch or U-turn users that can bring Diglett in, as Alolan Grimer is very vulnerable to it.
Alolan Grimer can pair well with the majority of setup sweepers of the tier: Nasty Plot Vullaby is an exceptional partner and forms a Dark-type core with Alolan Grimer. Vullaby appreciates Alolan Grimer's Knock Off and ability to remove Fairy-types thanks to its Poison typing; on the other hand, Alolan Grimer loves Vullaby's ability to switch into Ground-type moves. Shell Smash Tirtouga pairs well with Alolan Grimer because it can remove opposing Eviolites and check Grass-types; in exchange, Tirtouga checks some Ground-types and picks off Diglett when its Focus Sash has been broken. Alolan Grimer struggles a lot against Ground-types such as Diglett, Mudbray, and Hippopotas because they can KO it; powerful attackers with access to priority moves, such as Dragon Dance Corphish and Carvanha, make for great partners, picking off Diglett and severely denting Mudbray and Hippopotas. Cleric support is deeply appreciated because Alolan Grimer doesn't have a solid form of recovery besides Berry Juice and suffers from burns: Spritzee can be a good partner, providing both Wish and Aromatherapy support to heal Alolan Grimer; Snubbull can weaken physical attacks that target Alolan Grimer thanks to Intimidate and provide Heal Bell support to remove burns; Z-Memento Cottonee can restore Alolan Grimer's health when it is low, soften an opposing sweeper, and also take on the Ground-types that Alolan Grimer hates. Fighting-types appreciate Alolan Grimer as a Psychic-, Ghost-, and Fairy-type check; Timburr, Mienfoo, and Pancham pair well with it, removing the Steel-types that check it. Finally, Grass-types such as Foongus and Pumpkaboo-XL can check the Ground-types that threaten Alolan Grimer.
Rest is Alolan Grimer's form of recovery, fully restoring its HP and removing status ailments. Sleep Talk allows Alolan Grimer to attack while sleeping and turns it into a good Spore absorber. Knock Off is a must, as it is a STAB move that removes items such as Eviolite and Choice Scarf, and it also has a chance of poisoning thanks to Poison Touch. Poison Jab is Alolan Grimer's secondary STAB move, boasting an impressive 51% chance of poisoning the target while also hitting Fairy-types super effectively. On the other hand, Gunk Shot has a lower chance of poisoning than Poison Jab but packs more power; it can OHKO standard Spritzee after Stealth Rock and non-Eviolite Snubbull at -1 Attack while having a small chance to OHKO Eviolite Snubbull.
196 EVs in Attack and an Adamant nature make Alolan Grimer hit very hard, reaching 18 Attack. Eviolite boosts Alolan Grimer's defenses: with this item, it has a good chance to survive an Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Diglett while always surviving one from the Focus Sash variant; with its Special Defense, it has a very small chance of being 3HKOed by Focus Sash Abra's Dazzling Gleam while never being 2HKOed by the Life Orb variant. Poison Touch is Alolan Grimer's best ability because it can poison foes when making contact, which complements Poison Jab very well. An EV spread of 36 HP / 196 Atk / 36 Def / 36 SpA / 196 SpD lets Alolan Grimer check Abra and Gastly more reliably but loses some needed physical bulk; alternatively, a spread of 36 HP / 36 Atk / 196 Def / 36 SpA / 196 SpD grants better mixed bulk to avoid most OHKOs but at the cost of significant offensive presence.
Unlike the Pursuit trap set, this Alolan Grimer set can last longer with less support, as it can heal itself with Rest. Knock Off is the move to spam the most because it removes foes' items and has a good chance of poisoning. Alolan Grimer should enter the field on a move it resists or is immune to, such as Psychic- or Grass-type moves, because even though this set is quite bulky, it dislikes taking too much damage. It can come in on Psychic-types like Abra, Grass-types like Foongus and Pumpkaboo-XL, Ghost-types like Gastly, and Fairy-types like Spritzee. Thanks to Sleep Talk, Alolan Grimer can come in on Foongus and Morelull to absorb Spore; Foongus has nothing to threaten Alolan Grimer with, while Morelull is outsped and OHKOed by Alolan Grimer's Poison-type STAB move.
Even though Alolan Grimer can tank powerful hits, it has issues against Ground-types such as Mudbray and Diglett. This makes strong Water-type attackers with access to priority moves, such as Dragon Dance Corphish and Carvanha, great partners because they can pick off Diglett and severely hurt Mudbray. Entry hazard setters pair well with Alolan Grimer because it appreciates the chip damage provided by Stealth Rock and Spikes; defensive Tirtouga can set up Stealth Rock and, to a lesser extent, threaten Diglett with Aqua Jet; Ferroseed can set up Stealth Rock and Spikes; and Drilbur can set up Stealth Rock and remove entry hazards from Alolan Grimer's side of the field with Rapid Spin, while Alolan Grimer checks Grass-types for Drilbur. This Alolan Grimer variant depends less on Wish support than the Pursuit trap set, but a cleric can be used to heal Alolan Grimer when it is aslee or unable to use Rest; Spritzee or Snubbull can fill this role well. Grass-types can alleviate its weakness to Ground-type moves, making Pumpkaboo-XL and Foongus good teammates.
Giga Drain allows Alolan Grimer to heavily damage Onix in particular once its Sturdy has been broken, in addition to hitting Tirtouga, Omanyte, and Kabuto. Memento can be used when Alolan Grimer has done its job, reducing the opponent's offensive pressure and easing the setup of sweepers such as Nasty Plot Vullaby, Shell Smash Shellder, and Swords Dance Pawniard. Snarl can hit Abra and Gastly behind a Substitute, but Alolan Grimer's Special Attack is very low, meaning it won't hit hard. For the Berry Juice set, Thief can be used once Alolan Grimer's item has been used; however, Knock Off is usually better because it packs more power. Alolan Grimer can run a Rock Polish set, but it lacks the power to OHKO most foes and will be outsped by most Choice Scarf users even at +2 if it runs an Adamant nature. Stone Edge can be used to hit Flying-types such as Archen and Vullaby hard, but both dislike losing their items, and Alolan Grimer has issues fitting it into a set; the Pursuit trap set appreciates Shadow Sneak and Fire Punch more, and the RestTalk set has room only for its STAB moves. Curse can be used on the RestTalk set, allowing Alolan Grimer to boost its Attack and Defense; however, it has to forgo one of its STAB moves, which is hard to justify; if Alolan Grimer forgoes Knock Off, then Steel-types totally wall it; if it forgoes Poison Jab or Gunk Shot, then Fighting- and Fairy-types hard check it. Taunt can shut down opposing walls, but it's unreliable due to Alolan Grimer's low Speed and also because Alolan Grimer can damage walls with Knock Off.
Ground-types: Diglett is a nightmare for Alolan Grimer because it can trap and KO Alolan Grimer with Earthquake after Stealth Rock. Mudbray can take any hit from Alolan Grimer and retaliate with an Earthquake; RestTalk variants can also get around poison. Hippopotas can tank any hit from Alolan Grimer and KO it with Earthquake; Alolan Grimer also dislikes the sand damage and the possible Stealth Rock Hippopotas can set up. However, Hippopotas does not like being poisoned by Alolan Grimer's moves and hates losing its Eviolite.
Steel-types: Even though they do not appreciate Knock Off, Steel-types can check Alolan Grimer quite well. Pawniard is a prime example, as it completely stops the RestTalk set and can check the Pursuit trap set if it lacks Fire Punch. Magnemite does not appreciate Knock Off (especially Berry Juice variants) and gets 2HKOed by Fire Punch but can 2HKO Alolan Grimer with Thunderbolt or pivot out with Volt Switch, gaining momentum.
Rock-types: Rock-types resist Poison Jab and Gunk Shot, making it hard for Alolan Grimer to hit them hard. Onix can force Alolan Grimer, giving it opportunities to set up Stealth Rock. Archen resists Alolan Grimer's Poison-type moves and can threaten it with Earthquake but should be wary of Knock Off. Shell Smash users such as Omanyte and Tirtouga can use Alolan Grimer as setup bait because it lacks a solid option against them.
Croagunk: Croagunk stops Alolan Grimer no matter the set; it resists both of Alolan Grimer's STAB moves, is immune to poison by virtue of its typing, is only 3HKOed by Fire Punch even factoring in Dry Skin, and can use Alolan Grimer as setup bait for Nasty Plot or Bulk Up.
Residual Damage: The Pursuit trap set suffers from residual damage because it lacks a form of recovery besides Berry Juice. Weather damage such as from sand and hail, entry hazards such as Spikes and Stealth Rock, and burns constantly reduce Alolan Grimer's HP.

name: Muk
smogon_description:
Muk's high HP and Special Defense stats make it a good check to several special attackers in the metagame like Swanna, Silvally-Water, and Silvally-Dragon while also enabling to check common special setup sweepers that threaten stall teams like Servine, Raichu, and Simisage. Muk's access to Curse makes it a threatening setup sweeper for unprepared teams, exploiting passive Pokemon such as Altaria and Lickilicky. Furthermore, a very helpful ability in Sticky Hold, allows Muk to keep its item against Trick, Switcheroo, and Knock Off users, helping it check threats such as Rotom-S and Choice Specs Floatzel more reliably without being forced out. However, Muk struggles to beat Steel-types like Bronzor and Mawile with its STAB move, and while it has the option of running coverage moves like Fire Punch to beat them, doing so makes Muk a lot more passive.
Rest helps keep Muk healthy throughout the match to check special attackers better while also helping it get rid of status that would otherwise hinder its ability to sweep, such as Rotom-S's Will-o-Wisp. Fire Punch can be run over Poison Jab so Muk can get past Steel-types like Bronzor and Probopass, but it makes Muk a lot more passive and weaker offensively, making it hard to get past Fire- and Water-types such as Rapidash and Swanna while also missing on Poison Jab's high poison chance, which can be useful to cripple non-immune checks.
Leftovers is used over Black Sludge due to Pyukumuku's Soak making Black Sludge damage Muk. Moreover, since Muk's ability Sticky Hold prevents its item from being removed, it's actually impossible to punish Trick and Switcheroo users.
This set is a reliable switch-in to several special attackers in the metagame, being able to threaten them with a Curse setup, so it should be brought in to sponge a hit from these. It also switches into passive Pokemon like Altaria with ease. Due to this set being easily walled, using Poison Jab to try to get the 30% poison chance or double switching to a trapper or a wallbreaker is usually a good move early-game, allowing you to remove or pressure your opponent's answers to Muk. With Rest and a Poison typing, this set is an excellent status absorber, being able to switch into moves like Altaria's Toxic and Gourgeist-XL's Will-O-Wisp. Due to Sticky Hold, Muk can potentially come in on Trick and Switcheroo users like Floatzel and Rotom-S and force them out. Therefore, Muk should attempt to set up once its checks are either removed or crippled with status, potentially sweeping the opposing team. If using Fire Punch, it's wise to conceal Muk's attacking move, so it can surprise the opponent and break down its check in order to sweep at the right opportunity.
Good partners to Muk include trappers like Probopass, Alolan Golem, Silvally-Dark, and Pawniard, which can remove Steel- and Psychic-types that interfere with Muk's ability to sweep. Ground-immune as Altaria and Bronzor make good partners to Muk due to their ability to switch into Earthquake. Physically defensive Pokemon that don't share Muk's weaknesses like Gourgeist-XL, Beheeyem, and Gabite are also good teammates, being able to absorb super effective hits such as Golem's Earthquake that would otherwise heavily damage Muk due to its average Defense stat. On more balanced builds, wallbreakers like Komala and Pinsir make for good partners to this set, as they are able to remove Muk's common checks such as Bronzor and Mareanie, paving the way to a sweep.
On the Curse set, Brick Break is an option over Sleep Talk, being able to 2HKO trapper Probopass, which otherwise beats Muk with Tectonic Rage, while Ice Punch can be run to hit Ground-types such as Gabite, Sandslash, and Silvally-Ground. Due to Muk's good physical movepool, a Choice Band set is an option to potentially lure and remove common checks while wallbreaking using Gunk Shot's raw power, but this set is very reliant on predictions. On such a set, Thunder Punch is an option to hit Mareanie while Shadow Sneak can be used to revenge kill Psychic-types such as Kadabra and Mr. Mime. An Assault Vest set is also an option that capitalizes on Muk's special bulk while being able to lure and remove certain checks such as Probopass, but this set struggles to get past defensive Pokemon such as Gourgeist-XL, Altaria, and Lickilicky and is chipped rather easily due to its lack of recovery. Poison Touch can be used over Sticky Hold for the high poison chance alongside Black Sludge, but keeping Muk's item intact is usually better in the long run. Muk has access to trapping moves like Infestation and Block, so it can potentially run a set with Acid Spray and/or Toxic to lure and remove threats like Mareanie, Pyukumuku and Gourgeist-XL. It can also trap defensive Pokemon such as Altaria and set up on them.
Haze Mareanie: Haze Mareanie is the best Muk counter in the tier, removing Muk's Curse boosts and taking advantage of its passiveness towards it to set Toxic Spikes.
Spite Pyukumuku: Spite Pyukumuku can trap Muk with Block and PP stall it while ignoring its boosts due to Unaware. It also runs Rest so Muk can't afflict it with status or beat it during the process.
Steel-types: Steel-types like Mawile, Bronzor, and Probopass wall the mono-attacking set with Poison Jab, setting entry hazards or pivoting out to gain momentum. They need to watch out for Fire Punch, though. Trapper Probopass will beat Muk one-on-one regardless of Fire Punch if its Z-Move hasn't been used yet.
Ground-types: Ground-types like Golem, Sandslash, Silvally-Ground, and Gabite can all switch into Muk and proceed to beat it with their Ground-type STAB moves.
Psychic-types: Psychic-types with access to a strong STAB move like Kadabra, Mr.Mime and Beheeyem can all revenge kill unboosted Muk. Beheeyem can switch into Muk and proceed to set up or OHKO it most of the time with Shattered Psyche. Kadabra can threaten Muk with Counter due to Focus Sash and Magic Guard. Neither Mr. Mime nor Kadabra can afford to switch in on Muk, though.
Physical Wallbreakers: Strong physical wallbreakers like Electivire, Komala, Rampardos, and Pinsir can all beat even a boosted Muk with super effective coverage due to its average Defense stat.

name: Alolan Muk
smogon_description:
Alolan Muk's stellar defensive typing and above average special bulk let it be an excellent special tank and one of the best Pursuit trappers in the tier, capable of providing valuable support to teams by removing threats such as Latias, Chandelure, and Gengar. Knock Off in combination with Alolan Muk's ability Poison Touch can make a deadly combination, as many of its common switch-ins like Swampert and Krookodile are easily worn down when deprived of their item and poisoned. However, Alolan Muk's low physical bulk makes it easily exploitable by physical attackers like Cobalion, Terrakion, and Krookodile, although it does have some methods of punishing them if they try to set up on it. Alolan Muk is also extremely conscious of its health; if it is worn down, it is no longer able to threaten Pokemon like Calm Mind Latias. Also, Alolan Muk's low Speed means that it will almost always need to take a hit before attacking, which makes keeping it healthy throughout the game a somewhat difficult task. The combination of these traits means that Alolan Muk has a decent amount of competition as a Pursuit trapper from more offensive Pokemon such as Mega Aerodactyl, Krookodile, and Scizor, although its good bulk still makes it a staple as a Pursuit trapper.
Pursuit lets Alolan Muk trap and remove Psychic- and Ghost-types like Latias and Chandelure as well as reliably weaken other special attackers like Nihilego, Moltres, and Rotom-C. Gunk Shot is Alolan Muk's strongest attack, and it lets Alolan Muk OHKO Pokemon such as Mega Pidgeot after Stealth Rock and 2HKO Pokemon such as Hydreigon. Gunk Shot is also capable of pressuring Blissey more easily. Alternatively, Poison Jab can be used as a more accurate and more reliable Poison-type STAB attack that takes full advantage of Poison Touch with a combined 51% chance to poison foes. Knock Off is a general utility move that is also Alolan Muk's strongest Dark-type STAB attack; it can remove items from common switch-ins like Swampert and Rhyperior to punish them. Fire Punch lets Alolan Muk threaten Steel-types like Scizor and Klefki on the switch. Shadow Sneak is an alternative option over Fire Punch that lets Alolan Muk reliably switch in and beat Calm Mind Dragonium Z Latias, and it also can be used to pick off severely weakened threats more easily. Fire Blast is an alternative over Fire Punch that can deal more damage to Cobalion, but it does less damage than Fire Punch to Scizor and specially defensive Klefki and is also less accurate. Focus Punch lets Alolan Muk hit Terrakion, Cobalion, and Krookodile on the switch and deal heavy damage to Blissey if it uses a status move. However, the move is very tricky to use, so it's rather niche.
Maximum Attack investment with an Adamant nature lets Alolan Muk deal as much damage as possible. Maximum Special Defense EVs with an Assault Vest give Alolan Muk a very respectable amount of special bulk to check threats such as Celebi and Gengar more effectively. A Brave nature should be used if running Fire Blast so Alolan Muk's Special Attack is not decreased. Poison Touch gives all of Alolan Muk's contact attacks an additional chance to poison foes. Alolan Muk's spread is extremely customizable depending on the needs of the team; for example, it can run a bulkier spread of 252 HP / 112 Atk / 112 SpD / 32 Spe with an Adamant nature, which allows it to outspeed Swampert, take physical hits like Swampert's Earthquake and Cobalion's Close Combat better, and overall take less chip damage.
Keep Alolan Muk healthy in matchups where it can Pursuit trap foes such as Latias and Chandelure, as they can break through it easily if it takes too much damage beforehand. On the other hand, if there are no Pokemon that Alolan Muk will be particularly useful against, it can either be used as a sacrifice or attempt to spread poison and remove the items of foes with Knock Off until it is taken out. Alolan Muk needs to predict carefully against foes such as Calm Mind Latias and Calm Mind Chandelure; for example, if the foe has a boost from Calm Mind, Alolan Muk may want to consider using Knock Off rather than Pursuit for the increased damage output. Be aware, though, that +1 Dragonium Z Latias is capable of breaking past Alolan Muk anyway if it is healthy enough to survive a Knock Off. Sometimes, if Alolan Muk is in against a foe that it checks that doesn't threaten the team much, it may be best to let them switch out so that Alolan Muk can hit a predicted switch-in such as Swampert or Scizor with Knock Off or Fire Punch in order to cripple or KO them.
Pokemon such as Cobalion and Infernape that struggle against threats such as Latias, Chandelure, and Gengar heavily appreciate Alolan Muk's ability to Pursuit trap these threats. Setup sweepers like Scizor and Cobalion heavily appreciate the removal of specially offensive revenge killers like Chandelure and Alolan Muk's ability to soften up foes by poisoning them and removing their items. Grass- and Water-types like Celebi, Rotom-C, Suicune, and Starmie make good partners for Alolan Muk because they can deal with Ground-types like Rhyperior, Swampert, and Hippowdon. Checks to Fighting-types such as Chandelure and Doublade can beat foes such as Cobalion and Infernape that exploit Alolan Muk. Wish support from Pokemon such as Sylveon and Alomomola and entry hazard removal from Pokemon such as Mega Altaria, Mantine, and Rotom-C are very valuable for Alolan Muk so that it can stay healthy throughout the match. Volt Switch and U-turn users such as Rotom-C, Infernape, and Scizor can bring Alolan Muk in safely against several of the foes that it Pursuit traps.
Explosion can also be used, as it lets Alolan Muk KO or heavily damage a foe and gain momentum for the team when its job of Pursuit trapping is complete, but Explosion also leaves Alolan Muk unable to hit Klefki and other bulky Steel-types.
Physical Attackers: Physical attackers such as Terrakion, Cobalion, and Mega Aerodactyl can use Alolan Muk as setup bait and force it out with the threat of heavy damage.
Ground-types: Ground-types such as Swampert, Krookodile, and Hippowdon can easily take any of Alolan Muk's attacks and threaten it out with their super effective STAB attacks, although most of them are bothered by Knock Off.
Steel-types: Steel-types such as Scizor, Cobalion, and Mega Aggron can take most of Alolan Muk's attacks and force it out, but Scizor is eliminated by Fire Punch. Cobalion and Mega Aggron are especially notable, as Cobalion gains an Attack boost from Knock Off thanks to Justified and is not 2HKOed by Fire Punch, while Mega Aggron takes essentially nothing from any of Alolan Muk's attacks.
Residual Damage: Alolan Muk needs to be as healthy as possible in order to effectively Pursuit trap foes such as Latias and Chandelure, so residual damage from entry hazards such as Stealth Rock and U-turn users such as Celebi and Choice Scarf Hydreigon can make Alolan Muk rather ineffective at its role.
Lures: Pokemon such as Groundium Z Celebi can lure in Alolan Muk and KO it with their strong Z-Moves. If Alolan Muk is somewhat worn down, foes such as Calm Mind Dragonium Z Latias can also take it out. Some special attackers such as Rotom-H and Rotom-C can carry Will-O-Wisp to cripple Alolan Muk on the switch.

name: Shellder
smogon_description:
Possessing immense physical bulk and passable Speed and Attack, Shellder has the right traits to pull off a successful Shell Smash set. Being a pure Water-type is also beneficial for Shellder, not only giving it a great number of setup opportunities but also making it neutral or resistant to all priority attacks. Additionally, Skill Link gives Shellder an edge over most other Shell Smash users, as it allows Shellder to circumvent Focus Sash Abra without giving up an important coverage move. Skill Link has some interesting quirks in LC, making Icicle Spear and Rock Blast hit far harder than their already impressive 125 Base Power would imply. However, Shellder heavily relies on Shell Smash to become a threat and can hardly afford not to run the move.
Shell Smash makes Shellder super threatening, doubling both its Speed and its Attack. Icicle Spear and Rock Blast benefit from Skill Link, changing them from subpar attacks into Shellder's best offensive moves. Multi-hit attacks have some weird mechanics in LC, causing them to hit especially hard and be stronger than any of Shellder's STAB attacks. Moreover, Ice and Rock coverage is overall excellent, missing only Steel-types. Between just these two attacks, Shellder is truly an offensive threat and among the best sweepers in the tier. Liquidation is used to OHKO Mudbray and most Steel-types easily. Ice Shard can be run instead, primarily to KO Doduo and Diglett before they can use their strong priority options to revenge kill a weakened Shellder; however, Liquidation is generally better, as it makes Shellder far harder to wall.
Skill Link is what makes Shellder so deadly, guaranteeing its multi-hit moves always hit five times, thus dealing the most possible damage. In LC, multi-hit moves are even more powerful than their Base Power would indicate thanks to the intricacies of the damage formula, giving Shellder amazing power. Shellder opts for an Impish nature over an Adamant one in favor of increasing its Defense to improve its survivability and setup capabilities, which are further bolstered by an Eviolite. The Attack investment without a boosting nature is more than adequate anyway, as +2 Icicle Spear and Rock Blast have the same damage rolls as they would with an Adamant nature. The Speed investment allows +2 Impish Shellder to outspeed 17 Speed Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Mienfoo. A Jolly nature is also viable to allow Shellder to outspeed Scarf Doduo and Gastly after Shell Smash. The remaining EVs are invested into HP to give Shellder slightly better bulk.
As with any sweeper, Shellder's checks need to be weakened before it can sweep. Some troubling Pokemon need to be scouted for, such as Chinchou and Tirtouga, as Berry Juice variants check Shellder while other variants do not. Otherwise, using Shellder is rather straightforward: set up on a physical attacker, avoid setting up on a status user, and proceed to sweep.
Memento users, especially Cottonee and Diglett, pair well with Shellder, often giving it amazing setup chances and helping to keep it healthy enough to avoid being revenge killed. Diglett is also able to trap and weaken troubling Pokemon such as Chinchou and potentially Pawniard, while Cottonee is able to provide more utility through Knock Off support and act as a defensive pivot. Knock Off users are pretty good Pokemon to pair with Shellder too, as they remove Eviolites from the bulkiest Pokemon in the tier, allowing Shellder to blast through them. Vullaby is a great Knock Off user and is excellent at breaking down a number of checks it has in common with Shellder. Mienfoo and Timburr also pair well with Shellder, as they use Knock Off to remove Eviolites from some troubling Pokemon. More importantly, both are able to lure and exploit Croagunk and Snubbull, potentially removing one to make Shellder's sweep easier. Magnet Pull Magnemite is a decent partner that allows Shellder to drop Liquidation and run Ice Shard to prevent being revenge killed. Abra with Knock Off and Shadow Ball is a good wallbreaker for Shellder, as the set lures and beats Slowpoke and Honedge, two of the better, though uncommon, counters to Shellder. Lastly, Stealth Rock support is a necessity, making most reliable Stealth Rock users a good pairing. Hippopotas, Onix, and Pawniard are particularly good teammates due to helping fend off Electric-types and being the most reliable Stealth Rock users available.
Shellder has a few other options, though most are not worthwhile. Choice Scarf Shellder is one such example, but it lacks a niche due to Life Orb Staryu and Alolan Sandshrew being better fast Rapid Spin users. Choice Scarf Shellder may potentially catch a few Pokemon by surprise and revenge kill Pokemon behind Substitutes, but beyond this, its uses are limited. Staryu and Alolan Sandshrew also outclass a bulky Rapid Spin set, as both are able to KO Pumpkaboo attempting to spinblock, and, unlike them, Shellder struggles to switch into attacks. Shellder can use Rapid Spin as its fourth move on the Shell Smash set for role compression, but it necessitates a lot of support and is seldom worthwhile. Hidden Power Fighting can also be viable as the fourth attack, though it messes up Shellder's EV spread and leaves Shellder walled by some Mudbray sets with the only benefit being reliably KOing Pawniard and Magnemite. Hydro Pump is a decent option, KOing Mudbray if it switches into Rock Blast and doing more damage to Pawniard; however, it tends to miss at unideal times. Life Orb Shellder is the most viable other option at Shellder's disposal, though it requires Memento support to set up and its largest upsides are seldom useful unless Knock Off support cannot be afforded.
Slowpoke: Slowpoke survives any attack from even a boosted Shellder and stays healthy easily between Regenerator and Slack Off. Slowpoke is Shellder's largest issue, as even wearing it down is not enough thanks to Regenerator allowing for Slowpoke to switch in and heal at will.
Bulky Pokemon: Eviolite Spritzee proves to be an issue due to its massive bulk, but it cannot be hit by Knock Off lest a +2 Icicle Spear KO it. Similarly, Berry Juice Tirtouga and Chinchou can survive any one attack from +2 Shellder. Ferroseed is also able to defeat a boosted Shellder, though it needs to keep its HP high. Croagunk, while not especially bulky, is able to revenge kill with Vacuum Wave and can switch in on Liquidation or Rock Blast.
Choice Scarf Users with 18 Speed: 18 Speed Pokemon holding a Choice Scarf such as Gastly and Doduo are able to outspeed Shellder even after it has boosted, exploit its lowered defenses, and usually OHKO even from full health.
Intimidate: Shellder relies on being at +2 to secure KOs, making the likes of Snubbull and other Intimidate users problematic.
Steel-types: Liquidation is more than enough to handle a Magnemite set lacking Endure, but Endure + Recycle sets can be an issue. Similarly, Liquidation only KOes weakened Pawniard, so if kept healthy Pawniard is an adequate counter. Pawniard's Sucker Punch is threatening to Shellder as well, forcing weakened Shellder to try to avoid the priority attack. Honedge and Bronzor are bulky enough to also take little from Liquidation and therefore make good counters.
