name: Combusken
smogon_description:
Thanks to a good offensive typing and an amazing ability in Speed Boost, Combusken is an excellent wallbreaker and sweeper in ZU. It is easily capable of snowballing, with it only taking two turns to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and three to outspeed every Choice Scarf user as well. With good mixed attacking stats, Combusken can go special or physical, making it at least somewhat unpredictable. Thanks to its typing, Combusken is capable of beating traditional Fighting-type checks like Gourgeist-XL and Mr. Mime as well as Fire-type checks like Golem and Silvally-Water. However, Combusken is very frail, leaving it easily revenge killed by priority, especially by Aqua Jet from Swanna and Floatzel. In addition, its low base 55 Speed means that is it is very reliant on Protect and Speed Boost to outspeed a lot of Pokemon, for example leaving it outsped by Floatzel at +1 and Choice Scarf Electivire and Swanna at +2. Protect leaves it quite strapped for moveslots, which is an issue compounded by its poor movepool leaving it without a good physical Fighting-type move and reliant on Hidden Power and Z-Moves. Because of this, it very rarely has room to run Eviolite, exacerbating its already poor bulk.
Hidden Power Ice is Combusken's best move against Altaria, 2HKOing the common physically defensive variants and doing the same to specially defensive sets after Stealth Rock damage. Hidden Power Electric is another option to target Water-types, especially those that also resist Focus Blast like Swanna and Mareanie; however, the former takes a lot of damage from All-Out Pummeling and is 2HKOed by Life Orb-boosted Fire Blast after Stealth Rock, meaning it only usefully targets the latter. In general, targeting Altaria is more valuable. Protect synergizes very well with Speed Boost, guaranteeing Combusken gets at least one boost, often allowing it to outspeed Pokemon like Silvally formes and Swanna.
Fightinium Z is usually the preferred item, as it allows Combusken to break Pokemon like Silvally-Water with some chip damage as well as OHKO Pokemon like specially defensive Komala, Assault Vest Bouffalant, and Lickilicky, though it needs Stealth Rock damage for the latter two. It's also guaranteed to hit, which can be very useful in situations where risking Focus Blast's 70% accuracy is not desirable. Life Orb is an alternative if your team already has a Z-Move user. Notably, it allows Hidden Power Ice to 2HKO specially defensive Altaria without Stealth Rock damage and sometimes OHKO physically defensive variants after Stealth Rock while also granting a general damage boost to Combusken's STAB moves. However, Combusken is worn down very quickly by the item, and it has to rely on Focus Blast's shaky accuracy to break Fire-resistant Silvally formes, which is often not preferable.
Combusken should focus on breaking holes in the opponent's team by utilizing its solid coverage. If running Fightinium Z, it's important to consider carefully what foe to use it on. This will most commonly be a Pokemon like specially defensive Lickilicky or Silvally-Water, which can take either STAB move but loses to All-Out Pummeling. KOing such a Pokemon will often allow either Combusken or one of its teammates to sweep. In general, Combusken should be brought in via a safe switch, such as by a slow Volt Switch or U-turn from Pokemon like Alolan Golem and Komala, as its frailty means it rarely wants to take a hit. The major exception to this rule is Gourgeist-XL, which is almost entirely unable to dent Combusken; the worst it can do is use Leech Seed, so Combusken can generally switch into it for free to generate momentum. Be liberal with predictions. It is important to keep up momentum when Combusken is on the field, as getting into a disadvantageous matchup is very crippiling. Therefore, considering carefully whether your opponent will switch in a Pokemon like Silvally-Water and 2HKOing it on the switch is crucial. Protect has several uses. Of course, most important is the ability to guarantee a Speed boost against Pokemon like Komala, but it can also be used to scout against Choice Scarf users like Electivire. When using it, always carefully consider how many boosts you will need, as it is often more worth it to use an attack in order to wallbreak before using Protect the next turn, after your opponent switches to a faster threat.
Combusken pairs well with physical wallbreakers and sweepers like Swords Dance Silvally formes and Bulk Up or Choice Band Komala, as they can take care of special walls like Bronzor and Muk, allowing Combusken to wallbreak more easily. In exchange, Combusken threatens physical walls like Golem and Gourgeist-XL. Silvally formes and Choice Band Komala can also bring in Combusken with U-turn. Other Pokemon that can do so, such as Electivire and other Silvally formes, work well with Combusken too. Since Combusken relies on Stealth Rock to grab certain 2HKOs and OHKOs, most notably on Altaria, setters like Golem and Bronzor pair well with it. Combusken deals well with Gourgeist-XL, so Pokemon like the aforementioned Komala and Golem greatly appreciate its presence. Due to Combusken's weakness to Water-types, Pokemon that deal with them like Silvally-Water and Gourgeist-XL are solid teammates. Pokemon that reliably beat Altaria, like Komala and Electivire, are important, as Combusken is very weak to it. Both of these also consistently beat Mareanie. Other Pokemon that beat Mareanie, like Mr. Mime and Life Orb Kadabra, are solid partners as well. Since Combusken does not appreciate being worn down, especially if using Life Orb, entry hazard removers like Komala, Silvally formes, and Altaria work well with it.
Flare Blitz is Combusken's most powerful move and allows it to sweep much more easily due to its high Base Power. Most notably, at +2 Attack, it has a good chance to OHKO Gourgeist-XL, as well as Swanna after Stealth Rock. Sky Uppercut is Combusken's strongest Fighting-type STAB move, and though it is still not particularly strong, it synergizes well with Flare Blitz, notably threatening Pokemon like Golem and Rapidash. Protect synergizes well with Speed Boost to guarantee that Combusken can obtain the boosts it needs to outspeed its foes.
Firium Z is generally the best option, as Inferno Overdrive is incredibly powerful, notably allowing Combusken to KO physically defensive Altaria at +2 with Inferno Overdrive followed by Flare Blitz. In addition, it OHKOes Swanna after Swords Dance. Fightinium Z is another option to OHKO physically defensive Golem as well as Silvally-Water after Stealth Rock at +2.
In most games, this Combusken set should focus on sweeping late-game. While Combusken can OHKO or 2HKO almost every Pokemon in the metagame after a Swords Dance boost, its reliance on Flare Blitz means it gets worn down quickly. Thus, it is important that Pokemon like Muk and Gourgeist-XL are weakened significantly before attempting a sweep. Always plan the use of Combusken's Z-Move well. Not only is it a way to break through Pokemon Combusken otherwise couldn't beat, such as Altaria, it also is the only way for Combusken to have an accurate, powerful, and recoil-free STAB move. Since Combusken will usually be looking for a setup opportunity, it is important to identify which foes it can exploit. Examples of such foes include Gourgeist-XL and Leafeon, but there are several others depending on how healthy Combusken is. Especially against offensive teams, it is sometimes not necessary to set up to sweep, as Flare Blitz's power and Combusken's solid offensive typing already allow it to clean up such teams late-game. Sometimes, Combusken can be used as a wallbreaker instead of a sweeper, as it is easily capable of breaking through many Pokemon. It can be an especially effective wallbreaker when playing against bulkier teams that rely on cores like Bronzor + Gourgeist-XL. However, since it often gets worn down too quickly while setting up and by Flare Blitz recoil, it is generally better to preserve it for late-game.
Since Combusken generally needs the opposing team weakened before reliably sweeping and wants as little Flare Blitz recoil as possible, wallbreakers like Komala are welcome teammates,  weakening Gourgeist-XL reliably and, less reliably, Mareanie. Parting Shot from Silvally formes can give Combusken more opportunities to switch in and set up. Combusken struggles to break through Silvally-Water, especially without Fightinium Z, so Pokemon that reliably beat it like Assault Vest or specially defensive Komala are quite useful. Combusken appreciates entry hazard support from Pokemon like Golem, Bronzor, and Crustle in order to wear down the opposing team and achieve its KOs more easily. In a similar manner, Combusken appreciates Rapid Spin or Defog support from Pokemon like Komala, Altaria, and Silvally formes in order to avoid being worn down by entry hazards in addition to Flare Blitz recoil.
Low Kick can be used over Sky Uppercut on the Swords Dance set to have a perfectly accurate STAB move that does increased damage to Golem and Silvally formes, but it fails to deal significant damage to the notable Komala and Floatzel, which means Sky Uppercut is usually preferred. Thunder Punch is another option on the Swords Dance set to more easily beat Silvally-Water and other Water-types, but Combusken does not have any moveslots to spare. Substitute can be used over Protect on either of the sets to keep Combusken safe, but it is less reliable at allowing it to obtain Speed boosts and wears it down even faster. Combusken can function as an offensive Defogger, but it generally lacks the moveslots to do so effectively.
Water-types: Pokemon like Silvally-Water, Mareanie, and Pyukumuku are not easily broken by Combusken and can threaten it back with their super effective STAB moves or Toxic, while Swanna and Floatzel can easily take out Combusken with Aqua Jet if they decide to run it. In addition, Swanna can avoid an OHKO from any of Combusken's moves bar +2 Inferno Overdrive, allowing it to revenge kill.
Flying-types: While Combusken can break through Altaria, it needs to hit it on the switch with Hidden Power Ice on the special set lest it get stalled out by Roost, or it needs to hit its Z-Move correctly on the physical set. Other Flying-types like Swanna and Rotom-S are capable of taking most of Combusken's hits before OHKOing it with their STAB moves.
Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf users like Electivire, Pinsir, and Mr. Mime can outspeed even +2 Combusken and easily OHKO it. However, if Combusken obtains enough Speed boosts, and in the case of a full health Electivire, a Swords Dance boost, it will KO them instead. Meanwhile, Pokemon like Floatzel and Dugtrio can outspeed and OHKO +1 Combusken, and both can run Substitute to catch Combusken on a predicted Protect.
Psychic-types: Pokemon like Grumpig and physically defensive Beheeyem can take on one or both of Combusken's sets, especially after its Z-Move has been used, while Focus Sash Kadabra can revenge kill any set if it is at full health.

name: Blaziken
smogon_description:
Giratina Formes: Both Giratina formes are able to switch into Mega Blaziken and take any hit with ease thanks to their typing and great defensive stats. Giratina-O is able to threaten it back with Ghost- or Dragon-type STAB attacks, whereas Giratina can phaze it with Roar or Dragon Tail and cripple it with Toxic.
Water-types: Water-types such as Toxapex and Mega Slowbro can switch into Mega Blaziken with ease, as they take minimal damage from its STAB moves and Stone Edge. Toxapex can neutralize its boost from Swords Dance with Haze and set up Toxic Spikes on it, only having to worry about Earthquake, while Mega Slowbro can put Mega Blaziken on a timer with Toxic and stall it out with Slack Off. Primal Kyogre may not be able to switch into Mega Blaziken, but it can take one unboosted hit and OHKO back with a Water-type STAB move.
Zygarde-C: With its sky-high HP and great Defense, Zygarde-C is able to switch in, take any hit from Mega Blaziken, and KO it with Thousand Arrows or cripple it with Glare before phazing it with Dragon Tail.
Support Arceus Formes: Support Arceus formes like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Ground are able to take any one hit from Mega Blaziken, and the latter two OHKO back with STAB Judgment.
Lugia: Lugia is able to switch into any attack from Mega Blaziken and phaze it with Whirlwind. It can also stall Mega Blaziken out of Stone Edge PP, forcing it to KO itself with Flare Blitz recoil. However, with Stealth Rock up, +2 Stone Edge is able to OHKO Lugia due to losing its Multiscale protection.
Primal Groudon: Support sets of Primal Groudon are able to take +2 Low Kick from full HP and OHKO Mega Blaziken with Precipice Blades.
Faster Attackers: Faster threats such Choice Scarf users like Yveltal and Xerneas can outspeed Mega Blaziken and OHKO it without Speed boosts. Even if it is at +1 Speed, the aforementioned Pokemon are both able to take any unboosted hit from Mega Blaziken. Support Arceus formes like Arceus-Ground, Arceus-Fairy, Mega Salamence, and Mega Gengar can also outspeed Mega Blaziken and deal massive damage or OHKO it.
Ultra Necrozma: Ultra Necrozma can outspeed Mega Blaziken and OHKO it with Photon Geyser or Earthquake. It can take any hit apart from +2 Knock Off from Mega Blaziken, and it gets outpaced if Mega Blaziken obtains a Speed Boost.
Mega Salamence: Mega Salamence can outspeed and OHKO with Double-Edge if Mega Blaziken has not obtained a Speed boost. Even then, Mega Salamence is able to take an unboosted Stone Edge and OHKO back with Facade or Earthquake. However, with Stealth Rock up, Mega Blaziken can OHKO Mega Salamence with Stone Edge.
Priority: Priority users such as Marshadow, Extreme Killer Arceus, Rayquaza, and Deoxys-A can revenge kill Mega Blaziken once it is in range. Due to its mediocre bulk and the recoil from using Flare Blitz, this is somewhat easy to achieve.

name: Mudkip
smogon_description:
Mudkip struggles to justify itself a spot on competitive teams, due to a poor Speed tier and limited movepool. Although it possesses above-average stats all-around, Corphish and Carvanha are better Water-type attackers that bring additional coverage along with more potent offenses. Chinchou's Electric typing along with Staryu's access to reliable recovery make them better defensive options than Mudkip.
Mudkip should look to come in on threats, tank a hit, and then deal damage. However, even with an Eviolite, there are better Water-type tanks that have better coverage, and Mudkip's poor Special Attack means that Ice Beam is often not threatening enough against Grass types. Offensive Staryu, Carvanha, and Corphish all outclass Mudkip as more offensive Water-types.

name: Marshtomp
smogon_description:
Marshtomp's great defensive typing makes it a great wall and counter to Electabuzz. Gabite does compete in these roles, and it may appear to outclass Marshtomp with its better Speed and even better defensive typing. However, Marshtomp beating Ice Punch Electabuzz and checking Fire-types better makes it plenty worthwhile. With RestTalk, it can afford to take repeated hits and chip damage. It only needs Earthquake as an attack because, while it cannot harm most Flying- and Grass-types, using Stealth Rock when they switch in suffices as punishment. In the event the team can afford another Stealth Rock user, then Marshtomp could opt for Scald or Yawn instead to pressure foes with status, though neither are as effective as Stealth Rock. A mixed defensive EV spread works best, as Marshtomp does not need much special bulk to counter Electabuzz, whereas extra physical bulk helps with Raboot.
Defoggers and Rapid Spin users like Vullaby and Wartortle often switch into Marshtomp when it uses Stealth Rock. Switching to an offensive teammate like Electabuzz, Choice Band Raboot, and Fraxure as they clear Stealth Rock is a great way to bring them in safely and preserve momentum; if they don't go for removal, then Marshtomp at least secured Stealth Rock to punish them later on. As for Hattrem and its Magic Bounce, use Dark-types like Galarian Linoone, Vullaby, and Zweilous to beat it, as well as offensive partners like Lampent and Thwackey that can switch into Giga Drain with no problem. Defensive partners that resist Grass are also a must; physical walls like Roselia, Tangela, Ferroseed, and Koffing complement Marshtomp in this vein by checking Thwackey.
Thanks to an excellent defensive typing, Marshtomp excels as a special wall that checks Fire-types such as Lampent and Magmar, blocks pivoting attempts from Volt Switch Electabuzz, Klang, and Pikachu, and threatens foes with Earthquake. Toxic cripples common switch-ins such as Thwackey and Tangela. Alternatively, Yawn can be used to force switches and synergize with Stealth Rock to prevent Defoggers from removing entry hazards. It also punishes Ferroseed and Duosion, which are both immune to Toxic, from switching in. Marshtomp can also opt for a mixed spread of 252 HP / 152 Def / 104 SpD and an Impish nature to better handle Piloswine and Pikachu, while still avoiding a 2HKO from Life Orb Kadabra and a 3HKO from Electabuzz and Magmar.
Marshtomp should aim to use its typing to force switches and set up Stealth Rock early-game and then focus on walling special attackers. Physical walls such as Koffing, Tangela, and Gurdurr benefit from Marshtomp checking special wallbreakers such as Kadabra and Magmar; in return, they handle physical wallbreakers such as Thwackey and Gurdurr. Pokemon that provide entry hazard control like Gurdurr, Galarian Mr. Mime, and Vullaby keep Marshtomp from being quickly worn down by residual damage. As a wall that lacks reliable recovery, Marshtomp greatly appreciates support from Wish and Healing Wish users such as Clefairy and Hattrem. Pokemon that can check Grass-types such as Golbat, Magmar, and Koffing are solid partners, as they cover for Marshtomp's glaring 4x weakness.
Marshtomp can forgo utility to become a more reliable wall with Rest + Sleep Talk, but this usually requires that another teammate has Stealth Rock instead. Seismic Toss is a plausible replacement for one of its attacks for more consistent damage against Defoggers, especially when paired with Toxic, and it also breaks Rufflet's Substitute. Whirlpool has a niche when paired with Toxic or Yawn, as it allows Marshtomp to severely wear down a Pokemon or guarantees the sleep from Yawn.
Grass-types: Tangela and Thwackey can switch into Marshtomp's attacks and threaten it out with their Grass-type STAB attacks. Ferroseed can freely set up Spikes against Marshtomp.
Magic Bounce Users: Hattrem prevents Marshtomp from setting up Stealth Rock, reflects its status moves, and often carries Giga Drain.
Setup Sweepers: Rufflet and Duosion can use Marshtomp as setup fodder. The former has Substitute to avoid Marshtomp's status moves, while Duosion is immune to Toxic but must be wary of Yawn.
Residual Damage: Marshtomp is vulnerable to chip damage from entry hazards and status moves due to its lack of reliable recovery, which limits its ability to check offensive threats.

name: Swampert
smogon_description:
Offensively, Mega Swampert is the premier Mega Evolution choice on rain teams because of Swift Swim and its Electric immunity. It also has the ability to break down conventional rain checks such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and the rare Mantine due to its secondary STAB attack, Earthquake, and its array of coverage moves such as Superpower and Stone Edge. Mega Swampert can also provide great role compression because it is a Stealth Rock user that beats Mega Sableye. Defensively, Mega Swampert opens holes to Pokemon rain is already weak to, most notably Ash-Greninja, Keldeo, and double weather teams featuring Mega Charizard Y + Tyranitar. Mega Swampert suffers the same problem with other bulky physical attackers, as it is prone to chip damage from Rocky Helmet, Rough Skin, and Iron Barbs, meaning its bulk sometimes cannot be used practically. Mega Swampert is also dependent on rain to function, meaning it can only be used effectively when rain is active.
Waterfall is Mega Swampert's strongest move in the rain, and it is used over Aqua Tail because of its perfect accuracy and chance to flinch. Earthquake is Mega Swampert's secondary STAB move, which is used to hit common nuisances to rain teams such as Toxapex and Tapu Fini. Ice Punch is the coverage move of choice to nail Dragon- and Grass-types such as Mega Latias, Mega Latios, Tapu Bulu, and Tangrowth. Mega Swampert has a unique niche on rain teams, as it is a Stealth Rock user that defeats Mega Sableye. Mega Swampert can use another coverage move if this niche is not valued; Stone Edge prevents Pelipper from walling Mega Swampert, OHKOes Mega Charizard Y on the switch, and avoids Zapdos's Static, while Superpower can be used to KO Ferrothorn and Kyurem-B from a higher amount of health, revenge kills Kartana, and is its most reliable attack for Rotom-W. Substitute can be used to ease prediction, conserving rain turns, and making Mega Swampert harder to revenge kill. 8 Special Defense also lets Mega Swampert's Substitute live Toxapex's rain-boosted Scald.
Maximum Attack and Speed EVs are utilized to allow Mega Swampert to hit as hard and be as fast as possible. Damp is the preferred ability for its situational use of stopping Landorus-T and Mew from using Explosion. An Adamant nature is preferred to enhance Mega Swampert's wallbreaking abilities, possessing significantly better odds to 2HKO Mega Latias and Assault Vest Tangrowth after Stealth Rock. A Jolly nature is viable to outpace Choice Scarf Kartana, especially if running Superpower, and allows Mega Swampert to revenge kill boosted threats like Dragon Dance Mega Charizard X and Shift Gear Magearna. Mega Swampert misses out on a lot of power, however.
One of Mega Swampert's best traits as a Swift Swim user is its high bulk, yet it is generally best not to use this bulk because Mega Swampert will need its health to survive priority attacks from Pokemon such as Mega Mawile and Ash-Greninja and attacks from faster Choice Scarf users such as Greninja. Mega Swampert already finds itself vulnerable to forms of chip damage such as Spikes, Rocky Helmet, and Iron Barbs, as well as weaker attacks such as Tapu Koko's U-turn and Mega Medicham's Fake Out. Mega Swampert should also be kept away from status moves, as they make it useless or easier to deal when trying to dance around rain turns through continuous switching. Even though Mega Swampert is generally the team's Electric immunity, be careful of switching into Volt Switch users like Magearna, Tapu Koko, and Rotom-W, as it can get chipped down easily by their other attacks and even crippled by the latter's Will-O-Wisp, which significantly reduces its wallbreaking capabilities.
When Mega Swampert gets in for free, it should be played based on what the opponent's Mega Swampert checks are. If the opposition has solid checks to it, Mega Swampert should be focused on weakening its checks using its plethora of coverage moves to support a possible secondary sweeper such as Ash-Greninja. If the matchup is more in Mega Swampert's favor, play patiently and use teammates such as Ferrothorn and Tapu Koko more often, as Mega Swampert will want to stay healthy as possible. This is especially important if one decides to run a Jolly nature, as it will not be forced out by Pokemon such as Jirachi and Victini in an effort to conserve its health. Finally, Stealth Rock should be used on a predicted switch or if there is a Pokemon that indefinitely walls Mega Swampert such as physically defensive Tangrowth. It is also best to use Stealth Rock against Sableye stall teams once Mega Swampert has conditioned the opponent into thinking it will not use Stealth Rock. However, a mistimed Stealth Rock against Mega Sableye can spell doom for Mega Swampert's team.
Pelipper is a mandatory teammate because it provides free rain with its ability Drizzle while checking Keldeo, one of the best checks to Mega Swampert. It also creates free turns for Mega Swampert with its slow U-turn and by baiting in Electric-types such as Zapdos and Tapu Koko. Choice Specs Pelipper in particular breaks down a lot of Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with, making a Jolly nature more affordable. A secondary Pokemon that takes advantage of rain, preferably Manaphy or Ash-Greninja, is also recommended, as the combination of Mega Swampert and one of them can overwhelm a lot of rain checks. If Ash-Greninja is used, it is best to use Spikes, as Mega Swampert appreciates the hazard support so Pokemon such as Mew and Tapu Bulu can no longer safely switch in. Ferrothorn is a great utility Pokemon on rain teams, as its Fire-type weakness is halved, and it can set up Spikes or even Stealth Rock, the latter freeing up a moveslot on Mega Swampert. Landorus-T also frees up a moveslot for Mega Swampert due to it being a powerful offensive Stealth Rock user. It also removes bulky Grass- and Water-types with Supersonic Skystrike.
Mega Swampert appreciates some way to break Tangrowth, so Tornadus-T is a great teammate, wearing down Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with such as Rotom-W, Tapu Fini, and Ferrothorn and switches into Choice Scarf Kartana and Serperior. Tapu Koko is also a good teammate, as it gets a perfectly accurate Thunder under rain, and it provides free switches for Mega Swampert with U-turn. Tapu Lele is another good teammate, blocking priority and switching into a lot of Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with, namely Tangrowth and bulky Water-types such as Slowbro.
Rain Dance is a good option so Mega Swampert can set up the rain itself rather than relying on Pelipper. Mega Swampert can attempt a sweep by boosting its Attack with Power-Up Punch, but Mega Swampert usually prefers an extra coverage than to boost its Attack in specific situations. Toxic, especially in conjunction with Substitute, can be used to punish its checks such as Tangrowth, Rotom-W, and Slowbro.
Water-types: Most Water-types force out Mega Swampert due to the threat of their Scald burning it. Suicune, Alomomola, Slowbro, and Pelipper are the most notable. Choice Scarf Keldeo outspeeds Adamant Mega Swampert and forces Mega Swampert out due to its powerful Hydro Pump. Physically defensive Rotom-W can come in on Mega Swampert with little fear and neuter it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mantine completely walls Mega Swampert lacking Stone Edge. A healthy physically defensive Tapu Fini can put Mega Swampert at a very low amount of HP with the combination of Nature's Madness and Moonblast.
Grass-types: Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur, Tangrowth, Tapu Bulu, and Ferrothorn threaten Mega Swampert with their Grass-type STAB moves. Tapu Bulu, non-physically defensive Tangrowth, and Ferrothorn must watch out for coverage moves in Ice Punch and Superpower, however.
Faster Pokemon: Mega Swampert is not unbelievably fast without a Jolly nature and the use of a Jolly nature makes Mega Swampert much easier to deal with using Pokemon such as Tangrowth and Mew. Choice Scarf users such as Kartana and Victini can outpace an Adamant Mega Swampert and take it out with Leaf Blade and Final Gambit, respectively. Serperior outpaces even Jolly variants and OHKOes Mega Swampert with Leaf Storm. Mega Swampert can also be surprised by the use of Grass Knot on Choice Scarf Greninja. Finally, Mega Alakazam traces Swift Swim and can take out a weakened Mega Swampert with Psychic or once again surprise it with Grass Knot.
Ash-Greninja: While Ash-Greninja cannot directly switch in, Water Shuriken is boosted in the rain and is capable of taking 75% of Mega Swampert's health, which is a common range of health it finds itself in because of how Mega Swampert is vulnerable to chip damage from Rocky Helmet and Pokemon it switches into such as Tapu Koko.
Removing Rain: Mega Swampert is slow and lacks a powerful Water-type attack outside of the rain. Tyranitar, Alolan Ninetales, and Mega Charizard Y change the weather, and the latter two can force Mega Swampert out due their STAB attacks and coverage.

Mega Swampert suffers the same problem with other bulky physical attackers, as it is prone to chip damage from Rocky Helmet, Rough Skin, and Iron Barbs, meaning its bulk sometimes cannot be used practically. Mega Swampert is also dependent on rain to function, meaning it can only be used effectively when rain is active.
Waterfall is Mega Swampert's strongest move in the rain, and it is used over Aqua Tail because of its perfect accuracy and chance to flinch. Earthquake is Mega Swampert's secondary STAB move, which is used to hit common nuisances to rain teams such as Toxapex and Tapu Fini. Ice Punch is the coverage move of choice to nail Dragon- and Grass-types such as Mega Latias, Mega Latios, Tapu Bulu, and Tangrowth. Mega Swampert has a unique niche on rain teams, as it is a Stealth Rock user that defeats Mega Sableye. Mega Swampert can use another coverage move if this niche is not valued; Stone Edge prevents Pelipper from walling Mega Swampert, OHKOes Mega Charizard Y on the switch, and avoids Zapdos's Static, while Superpower can be used to KO Ferrothorn and Kyurem-B from a higher amount of health, revenge kills Kartana, and is its most reliable attack for Rotom-W. Substitute can be used to ease prediction, conserving rain turns, and making Mega Swampert harder to revenge kill. 8 Special Defense also lets Mega Swampert's Substitute live Toxapex's rain-boosted Scald.
Maximum Attack and Speed EVs are utilized to allow Mega Swampert to hit as hard and be as fast as possible. Damp is the preferred ability for its situational use of stopping Landorus-T and Mew from using Explosion. An Adamant nature is preferred to enhance Mega Swampert's wallbreaking abilities, possessing significantly better odds to 2HKO Mega Latias and Assault Vest Tangrowth after Stealth Rock. A Jolly nature is viable to outpace Choice Scarf Kartana, especially if running Superpower, and allows Mega Swampert to revenge kill boosted threats like Dragon Dance Mega Charizard X and Shift Gear Magearna. Mega Swampert misses out on a lot of power, however.
One of Mega Swampert's best traits as a Swift Swim user is its high bulk, yet it is generally best not to use this bulk because Mega Swampert will need its health to survive priority attacks from Pokemon such as Mega Mawile and Ash-Greninja and attacks from faster Choice Scarf users such as Greninja. Mega Swampert already finds itself vulnerable to forms of chip damage such as Spikes, Rocky Helmet, and Iron Barbs, as well as weaker attacks such as Tapu Koko's U-turn and Mega Medicham's Fake Out. Mega Swampert should also be kept away from status moves, as they make it useless or easier to deal when trying to dance around rain turns through continuous switching. Even though Mega Swampert is generally the team's Electric immunity, be careful of switching into Volt Switch users like Magearna, Tapu Koko, and Rotom-W, as it can get chipped down easily by their other attacks and even crippled by the latter's Will-O-Wisp, which significantly reduces its wallbreaking capabilities.
When Mega Swampert gets in for free, it should be played based on what the opponent's Mega Swampert checks are. If the opposition has solid checks to it, Mega Swampert should be focused on weakening its checks using its plethora of coverage moves to support a possible secondary sweeper such as Ash-Greninja. If the matchup is more in Mega Swampert's favor, play patiently and use teammates such as Ferrothorn and Tapu Koko more often, as Mega Swampert will want to stay healthy as possible. This is especially important if one decides to run a Jolly nature, as it will not be forced out by Pokemon such as Jirachi and Victini in an effort to conserve its health. Finally, Stealth Rock should be used on a predicted switch or if there is a Pokemon that indefinitely walls Mega Swampert such as physically defensive Tangrowth. It is also best to use Stealth Rock against Sableye stall teams once Mega Swampert has conditioned the opponent into thinking it will not use Stealth Rock. However, a mistimed Stealth Rock against Mega Sableye can spell doom for Mega Swampert's team.
Pelipper is a mandatory teammate because it provides free rain with its ability Drizzle while checking Keldeo, one of the best checks to Mega Swampert. It also creates free turns for Mega Swampert with its slow U-turn and by baiting in Electric-types such as Zapdos and Tapu Koko. Choice Specs Pelipper in particular breaks down a lot of Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with, making a Jolly nature more affordable. A secondary Pokemon that takes advantage of rain, preferably Manaphy or Ash-Greninja, is also recommended, as the combination of Mega Swampert and one of them can overwhelm a lot of rain checks. If Ash-Greninja is used, it is best to use Spikes, as Mega Swampert appreciates the hazard support so Pokemon such as Mew and Tapu Bulu can no longer safely switch in. Ferrothorn is a great utility Pokemon on rain teams, as its Fire-type weakness is halved, and it can set up Spikes or even Stealth Rock, the latter freeing up a moveslot on Mega Swampert. Landorus-T also frees up a moveslot for Mega Swampert due to it being a powerful offensive Stealth Rock user. It also removes bulky Grass- and Water-types with Supersonic Skystrike.
Mega Swampert appreciates some way to break Tangrowth, so Tornadus-T is a great teammate, wearing down Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with such as Rotom-W, Tapu Fini, and Ferrothorn and switches into Choice Scarf Kartana and Serperior. Tapu Koko is also a good teammate, as it gets a perfectly accurate Thunder under rain, and it provides free switches for Mega Swampert with U-turn. Tapu Lele is another good teammate, blocking priority and switching into a lot of Pokemon Mega Swampert struggles with, namely Tangrowth and bulky Water-types such as Slowbro.
Rain Dance is a good option so Mega Swampert can set up the rain itself rather than relying on Pelipper. Mega Swampert can attempt a sweep by boosting its Attack with Power-Up Punch, but Mega Swampert usually prefers an extra coverage than to boost its Attack in specific situations. Toxic, especially in conjunction with Substitute, can be used to punish its checks such as Tangrowth, Rotom-W, and Slowbro.
Water-types: Most Water-types force out Mega Swampert due to the threat of their Scald burning it. Suicune, Alomomola, Slowbro, and Pelipper are the most notable. Choice Scarf Keldeo outspeeds Adamant Mega Swampert and forces Mega Swampert out due to its powerful Hydro Pump. Physically defensive Rotom-W can come in on Mega Swampert with little fear and neuter it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mantine completely walls Mega Swampert lacking Stone Edge. A healthy physically defensive Tapu Fini can put Mega Swampert at a very low amount of HP with the combination of Nature's Madness and Moonblast.
Grass-types: Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur, Tangrowth, Tapu Bulu, and Ferrothorn threaten Mega Swampert with their Grass-type STAB moves. Tapu Bulu, non-physically defensive Tangrowth, and Ferrothorn must watch out for coverage moves in Ice Punch and Superpower, however.
Faster Pokemon: Mega Swampert is not unbelievably fast without a Jolly nature and the use of a Jolly nature makes Mega Swampert much easier to deal with using Pokemon such as Tangrowth and Mew. Choice Scarf users such as Kartana and Victini can outpace an Adamant Mega Swampert and take it out with Leaf Blade and Final Gambit, respectively. Serperior outpaces even Jolly variants and OHKOes Mega Swampert with Leaf Storm. Mega Swampert can also be surprised by the use of Grass Knot on Choice Scarf Greninja. Finally, Mega Alakazam traces Swift Swim and can take out a weakened Mega Swampert with Psychic or once again surprise it with Grass Knot.
Ash-Greninja: While Ash-Greninja cannot directly switch in, Water Shuriken is boosted in the rain and is capable of taking 75% of Mega Swampert's health, which is a common range of health it finds itself in because of how Mega Swampert is vulnerable to chip damage from Rocky Helmet and Pokemon it switches into such as Tapu Koko.
Removing Rain: Mega Swampert is slow and lacks a powerful Water-type attack outside of the rain. Tyranitar, Alolan Ninetales, and Mega Charizard Y change the weather, and the latter two can force Mega Swampert out due their STAB attacks and coverage.

name: Poochyena
smogon_description:
Poochyena is a mediocre Pokemon. Even with boosts, Poochyena cannot do any damage, is very slow, is easily revenge killed due to its poor bulk, and has a poor movepool to boot. Being heavily outclassed by Vullaby and Pawniard as a Dark-type is not doing Poochyena any favors as well. Since it lacks much offensive and defensive utility, Poochyena should never be used on a serious team.
This set attempts to set up with Z-Howl, which gives it +2 Attack, after taking a Knock Off to boost its Speed via Rattled; however, due to Poochyena's horrid stats, it will be easily revenge killed and won't be able to do much damage or even have an opportunity to set up. Poochyena is fully outclassed by Vullaby and Pawniard, both being premier offensive and defensive Pokemon, especially the former, and providing way better offensive and defensive utility.

name: Mightyena
smogon_description:
Subpar stats across the board leave Mightyena completely outclassed by Absol and Alolan Raticate, which sport far higher Attack stats and better Speed tiers. The aforementioned Pokemon also have access to Swords Dance and possess a more useful Dark-type STAB move in Knock Off. Mightyena's niche lies in attempting to revenge kill opposing Pokemon to get Attack boosts from Moxie, but it does not do its job properly because it ends up being too weak to defeat anything and it lacks the defenses to stay in for long periods of time.
This set attempts to hit as hard as possible in order to revenge kill weakened Pokemon to achieve Moxie boosts, utilizing its STAB priority and coverage to attempt to beat checks. Unfortunately, Mightyena is outsped by a lot of offensive Pokemon and relies too much on Sucker Punch as an attacking move, being unable to use its good coverage. Alolan Raticate, for example, is a much better Pokemon to use because it has Swords Dance, Hustle, Normal-type STAB moves, and a better Speed tier. It also can use a Z-Move so it doesn't need to beat opposing Pokemon to become an immediate threat. It is advised to use Alolan Raticate and Absol as offensive Dark-type Pokemon over Mightyena.

name: Zigzagoon
smogon_description:
In Little Cup, Zigzagoon can act as an effective physical sweeper thanks to its access to the amazing combination of Belly Drum to maximize its Attack in an instant and Extreme Speed to outprioritize its foes and KO them. Unfortunately, it is hindered by its numerous flaws such as its poor bulk, which makes it struggle to set up Belly Drum reliably. Zigzagoon also requires excessive team support to perform its role with success, and without this, many Pokemon are able to get in the way of its sweep. In most games, Zigzagoon tends to either win the battle for its team with a successful sweep or fail to contribute anything at all.
Belly Drum turns Zigzagoon into a powerful sweeper, maximizing its Attack. Extreme Speed is the STAB move that Zigzagoon will be using the majority of the time in order to KO its foes. Its incredibly useful +2 priority compensates for Zigzagoon's low Speed stat, allowing it to sweep. Thief enables Zigzagoon to hit Ghost-types such as Gastly and Pumpkaboo-XL super effectively and can steal items once Berry Juice has been consumed. Seed Bomb provides coverage for Mudbray along with Rock-types like Onix and Tirtouga, though Protect is an alternative option that prevents Zigzagoon from being KOed by Fake Out users.
Berry Juice restores Zigzagoon's HP to ensure it can use Belly Drum without it failing, or in some cases it can restore Zigzagoon's HP after Belly Drum to prepare itself for taking a hit. An Adamant nature is utilized in conjunction with 196 Attack EVs so as to maximize Zigzagoon's Attack stat in order to KO as many Pokemon as possible. EVs are invested into bulk so that Zigzagoon can set up more reliably, and the remaining EVs are dumped into Speed.
Zigzagoon is best used towards the end of the battle once its checks and counters have been removed so that it can sweep without trouble. Zigzagoon should refrain from switching in on attacks because it has very low defensive stats and it can be difficult to set up once Berry Juice has been consumed. This means Zigzagoon should be brought in to battle via a free switch from the likes of a slow VoltTurn user or immediately after a teammate has fainted. Additionally, Zigzagoon should wait for an opportune time to set up. This is usually when the foe cannot stop Zigzagoon from using Belly Drum, KO Zigzagoon, or burn Zigzagoon.
Being frail, Zigzagoon appreciates Memento support from Pokemon like Diglett and Cottonee, as they can lower a foe's offensive stats and then give Zigzagoon a free switch, allowing it to set up safely. Diglett is arguably Zigzagoon's best teammate option, as not only can it provide Memento support, but it can also trap and KO Steel- and Rock-type Pokemon that resist Extreme Speed. It additionally has access to Stealth Rock. Entry hazard support like Stealth Rock is great because it can break Sturdy and Focus Sashes while also providing chip damage to make opposing Pokemon easier to KO for Zigzagoon. Other Pokemon that provide entry hazards include Dwebble and Onix. Pursuit users are also great partners because they can trap and remove Ghost-types and break Abra's Focus Sash, both of which otherwise cause trouble for Zigzagoon. Alolan Grimer and Stunky are especially good options, as they also provide Memento support. Knock Off users such as Pawniard and Mienfoo also help Zigzagoon sweep by removing bulky Pokemon's Eviolites so that Zigzagoon can KO them later. Furthermore, Pokemon that lure in Gastly, Zigzagoon's main Ghost-type threat, support Zigzagoon because it can then be Pursuit trapped. Likewise, Pokemon that lure in and weaken Steel-types are helpful for Zigzagoon. Snivy and the aforementioned Cottonee are great examples of these, luring in both Gastly and Steel-types.
Iron Tail can be used to grant Zigzagoon the ability to OHKO Spritzee, defensive Archen, and Lileep, while Rock Smash similarly is an option to OHKO Aron and Shieldon once Sturdy has been broken. These are not great choices, however, as these Pokemon are not very common and can be weakened beforehand. Normalium Z can be used instead of Berry Juice to allow Zigzagoon to use Z-Belly Drum, which restores its HP fully just before Belly Drum is used. This means that Zigzagoon can set up on Knock Off users; however, most Knock Off users threaten Zigzagoon anyway with their offensive power or typing. Normalium Z is also flawed because it guarantees that Zigzagoon will only have 50% or less of its HP remaining after Belly Drum, unlike when using Berry Juice. Return can also be utilized to OHKO bulky Pokemon such as Mareanie and Spritzee, but this means Zigzagoon will be missing out on important coverage.
Faster Ghost-type Pokemon: Ghost-types that outspeed Zigzagoon like Gastly are significant threats because of their immunity to Extreme Speed. They can attack or burn Zigzagoon before it gets the opportunity to use Thief.
Steel-type Pokemon: Steel-type Pokemon resist Extreme Speed, so they are sometimes able to survive an Extreme Speed and stop Zigzagoon's sweep. Pawniard is especially notable because it is able to Knock Off Zigzagoon's Berry Juice to prevent it from using Belly Drum, while it can also discourage Zigzagoon's teammates from using Memento, as it could switch in and gain an Attack boost from Defiant. Ferroseed is also a great threat, since Zigzagoon has no way to deal any considerable damage to it.

name: Linoone
smogon_description:
Linoone is the only Pokemon with access to both Belly Drum and Extreme Speed, making it a unique cleaner and sweeper in UU. Linoone is able to outspeed and beat most bulky Pokemon after setting up due to its coverage moves, Seed Bomb and Stomping Tantrum, that can KO most Pokemon resistant to Extreme Speed. Linoone's ability Gluttony, with a Figy Berry, means Linoone can almost always use Belly Drum. However, even after using Belly Drum, Linoone is revenge killed by every faster Normal-resistant or -immune Pokemon such as Cobalion, Gengar, and Scizor, which uses Bullet Punch to deal massive damage. Because of its low defensive stats, Linoone can be OHKOed by many offensive threats, which makes setting up against offensive teams difficult even at full health. Furthermore, Linoone's subpar stats leave it outclassed by other setup sweepers that use priority moves like Bisharp and Scizor. Linoone is a one-time sweeper that is utterly useless before setting up and is quite frail.
Belly Drum increases Linoone's Attack to +6, which makes it an extremely powerful offensive threat. Extreme Speed is a strong +2 priority STAB attack that OHKOes Pokemon such as Latias, Infernape, and Hydreigon after a boost from Belly Drum. Linoone also has great coverage moves that allow it to break through Normal-resistant walls: Seed Bomb, which lets Linoone break through bulky Water-types like Swampert, Suicune, and Quagsire that are not OHKOed by +6 Extreme Speed, and Stomping Tantrum, which allows Linoone to damage slow and bulky Steel-types like Mega Aggron and Mega Steelix; however, it does not OHKO them even at +6.
16 Speed EVs are used to outspeed Adamant Bisharp so Linoone can OHKO it with Stomping Tantrum. Linoone also Speed ties with Timid Primarina and Jolly Bewear. The HP, Defense, and Special Defense EVs make it so Linoone survives Mega Aerodactyl's Stone Edge, Latias's Draco Meteor, and Choice Band Scizor's Bullet Punch after Stealth Rock. The defensive investment also allows it to survive Hydreigon's Draco Meteor and Choice Band Scizor's U-turn from full HP. A Figy Berry combined with Gluttony allows Linoone to use Belly Drum once and completely recover all of the lost HP or take any one hit that would not OHKO it and gives it enough HP to use Belly Drum.
Linoone is only used as a late-game sweeper. For Linoone to be an effective sweeper, all faster threats that are immune to or resist Extreme Speed must be KOed or severely weakened. These threats include fast Ghost-types like Gengar, Steel-types like Cobalion, and Rock-types like Mega Aerodactyl. Linoone should not switch directly into any attacks or offensive threats. Instead, bring it in to set up either after a teammate has fainted or with the support of a Volt Switch or U-turn user against Pokemon that cannot OHKO Linoone.
Linoone is most effective on hyper offense. Specifically, Linoone thrives on dual screens offense due to the increased number of setup opportunities the playstyle provides. Azelf and Xatu are the only viable dual screens setters in the tier, so they make good partners. Linoone is very frail, so checks to Fighting-types, such as Latias and Mega Altaria, pair very well with it. Scizor threatens Linoone greatly, so checks to it such as Chandelure and Feraligatr make good partners. Choice Scarf Chandelure is particularly useful because it can use Memento to help Linoone set up. Linoone also appreciates support from stallbreakers like Lucario and Mega Altaria that weaken walls and allow Linoone to clean more easily. Fighting-types like Terrakion, Cobalion, and Infernape also pair nicely with Linoone because they are able to beat the Rock- and Steel-types that check it. Mega Manectric is a good teammate for Linoone because it can pressure physical attackers with Intimidate, check Steel-types, and use Volt Switch to bring Linoone in safely.
Linoone can run more Speed to outspeed Pokemon like Primarina. Specifically, 196 Speed EVs allow Linoone to outspeed Pokemon such as Tsareena, Chandelure, and Mega Blastoise.
Bulky Steel-types: Pokemon such as Mega Aggron, Cobalion, Doublade, Steelix, and Scizor are able to reliably take any attack from Linoone and KO or heavily damage it in return.
Faster Normal-resistant and -immune Pokemon: Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Cobalion, and Terrakion cannot be OHKOed by +6 Extreme Speed and OHKO Linoone in return. Chandelure and Gengar are immune to Extreme Speed and can outspeed Linoone and revenge kill it.

name: Galarian Linoone
smogon_description:
This set capitalizes on Galarian Linoone's fantastic utility movepool to shut down common walls such as Galarian Corsola and Ferroseed. Knock Off is a very coveted move in the tier, as it can remove Eviolite from defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Corsola, Tangela, and Mareanie, making them significantly less bulky and easier to deal with. Double-Edge is Galarian Linoone's best Normal STAB attack, hitting most of the tier for neutral damage and threatening Pokemon that tend to switch in on Knock Off such as Gurdurr. Taunt can be used to further cripple the aforementioned defensive walls, stopping them from getting up their respective entry hazards whilst also preventing them from spreading status. Parting Shot lets Galarian Linoone act as a pivot that can also weaken common wallbreakers such as Machoke.
Pokemon that are able to switch into strong Fighting-types such as Gurdurr and Machoke make for great partners. These include physical walls like Galarian Corsola, Tangela, Koffing, and Clefairy. Galarian Corsola in particular makes for an exceptional partner to Galarian Linoone, as it can deal with strong wallbreakers whilst also providing entry hazard support, while Galarian Linoone is able to knock out checks to Galarian Corsola such as Hattrem and Gastly. Pokemon that are able to provide speed control or Sticky Web support such as Charjabug and Thunder Wave Clefairy tend to be good partners for Galarian Linoone to help it break past faster wallbreakers such as Abra and Choice Scarf Raboot. Pokemon with access to U-turn like Raboot and Thwackey also complement Galarian Linoone very well, as they form a pivoting core that helps create momentum in a battle.
This set is a viable option to capitalize on Galarian Linoone's ability Quick Feet in conjuction with STAB Facade. As one of the fastest Pokemon in the tier, Galarian Linoone is able to use its STAB-boosted Facade offensively and revenge kill many threats such as Wartortle and Raboot. Protect gives Galarian Linoone a much easier time activating its Toxic Orb while also allowing it to stall out turns of Sun or Grassy Terrain. Switcheroo can be used to cripple switch-ins like Vullaby, Tangela, and physically defensive Machoke. Taunt lets it shut down common defensive Pokemon that rely on status moves like Galarian Corsola and Mareanie. Parting Shot gives Galarian Linoone an opportunity to switch out on its checks while making them weaker and easier to switch into.
This set synergizes extremely well with strong wallbreakers that struggle with Galarian Corsola such as Gurdurr and Thwackey, as well as being able to knock out threats such as Lampent for defensive walls like Koffing and Tangela. Clerics such as Clefairy and Hattrem are especially notable partners, as they are also able to give Galarian Linoone much more longevity with the use of Wish and Healing Wish. Volt Switch and U-turn users such as Klang, Thwackey, and Electabuzz form VoltTurn cores with Galarian Linoone, which helps keep momentum in a battle, making them exceptional partners. Try to pivot into special wallbreakers that break through Machoke and Tangela, with Electabuzz and Lampent being great teammates for the job.
Choice Band sets give more breaking power to Galarian Linoone, and let it also take advantage of Switcheroo to cripple walls. Choice Scarf works for that aspect as well, although it is usually inferior to Toxic Orb sets due to the Choice-lock and innability to take advantage of Facade. Thunder Wave is an option for speed control that works well to deter Counter Abra and Shell Smash Wartortle.
Fighting-types: By resisting Knock Off, Fighting-types like Machoke and Combusken are ample switch-ins to Galarian Linoone, and Gurdurr especially threatens it with its priority Mach Punch.
Physical Walls: Pokemon that function even after being hit by Taunt and Knock Off like Tangela, Clefairy, and Koffing prevent Galarian Linoone from capitalizing against them while they wear it down.
Slow Pivots: Defensive pivots like Charjabug, Vullaby, and Wartortle tank Galarian Linoone's attacks, and have pivoting attacks themselves to gain momentum against it.
Revenge Killers: Focus Blast from Electabuzz OHKOes Eviolite Galarian Linoone. Toxic Orb sets usually won't have to worry about faster Pokemon, but strong priority attackers like Thwackey and Piloswine become more of an issue.

name: Dustox
smogon_description:
With its two 4x resistances to Grass and Fighting, an immunity to Toxic, and access to both Quiver Dance and Iron Defense, Dustox can slowly turn into a setup sweeper. However, its typing brings forth several notable weaknesses, most notably to Fire, Flying, and Rock, that allow Dustox to be overcome by threats such as Simisear, Dodrio, and Aggron. Dustox also faces fierce competition from Bellossom as a bulky Quiver Dance sweeper, as Bellossom has better offensive stats as well as Strength Sap to restore its health while lowering the target's Attack.
Dustox can use its combination of Quiver Dance + Iron Defense + Roost to set up on Pokemon such as non-Stone Edge Hitmonchan. Once Dustox has obtained enough boosts, it can theoretically become a bulky sweeper; however, odds are Dustox will not be given such a chance to set up all the way due to its mediocre defensive stats, proving how much better Bellossom is as a bulky Quiver Dance sweeper despite Dustox's niches such as Shield Dust and its immunity to Toxic.

name: Lotad
smogon_description:
Lotad differentiates itself from other Swift Swim users with its perfect neutral coverage and key neutralities to Electric- and Grass-type attacks. However, with such abysmal stats across the board, Lotad is still a dysfunctional Swift Swim user, facing fierce competition for teamslots from Pokemon such as Omanyte and Mantyke. Furthermore, rain hyper offensive playstyles are exceedingly rare, making it even harder for Lotad to find its way onto teams. Lastly, Lotad is picked off easily by priority attackers such as Timburr due to its lack of Eviolite and terrible bulk. Lotad is also exceedingly slow, outsped by Choice Scarf users such as Pawniard even under rain.
Lotad should try to utilize its perfect neutral coverage to fire off as many attacks as possible under the limited duration of rain. However, this is easier said than done, as Lotad's exceedingly poor bulk limits it from ever directly switching in, mandating team support beyond what other Swift Swim abusers such as Kabuto and Omanyte need. Lotad is rather weak, however, making the support it requires not worthwhile when significantly better options exist.

name: Ludicolo
smogon_description:
Ludicolo is a fearsome sweeper in the PU metagame by virtue of its access to Swift Swim, which allows it to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame under rain. Furthermore, a decent Special Attack stat in tandem with a good STAB combination and nearly unresisted coverage allows it to adequately pressure offensive and defensive teams alike, and a fairly decent defensive typing and good special bulk allow it to tank some hits and find easy opportunities to set up on Pokemon like Floatzel and Lanturn. Unfortunately, Ludicolo is hindered by its poor Defense and Speed stats, as they can complicate setup and leave it susceptible to common threats in Skuntank, Primeape, and Scyther. It also suffers from the prevalence of Pokemon that can tank a hit in the rain and cripple or KO it in return, including Roselia and Assault Vest Hitmonchan. Lastly, Ludicolo's physical frailty can leave it prone to getting revenge killed by strong priority users, including Absol, Alolan Raticate, and especially Kangaskhan, which can stall out rain turns with Fake Out.
Rain Dance is mandatory for doubling Ludicolo's Speed and beginning a sweep, and it also supports some of Ludicolo's other teammates on dedicated rain teams. Hydro Pump is a powerful STAB attack that hits obscenely hard in the rain, OHKOing or 2HKOing the majority of neutral targets. Giga Drain allows Ludicolo to recover its health and is also useful for hitting Water-types such as Gastrodon and Lanturn. Energy Ball is an option over Giga Drain for its greater power, notably damaging the likes of Primeape and Swanna more reliably. Ice Beam hits the Grass- and Dragon-types that otherwise wall Ludicolo, including Lurantis, Victreebel, and Drampa. Focus Blast is an option over Rain Dance in order to hit Pokemon like Type: Null and Cradily harder, but it is unreliable and makes Ludicolo reliant on teammates to set up rain.
Full investment in both Special Attack and Speed maximizes Ludicolo's offensive presence. 29 IVs are invested in HP to minimize damage taken from Life Orb. A Modest nature is used to maximize Ludicolo's damage output, but Timid is also an option to outspeed faster Choice Scarf users such as Manectric and Scyther. Life Orb puts even more power behind Ludicolo's attacks, allowing it to secure KOs such as the 2HKO on Lanturn with Giga Drain.
Ludicolo should look to set up against Pokemon that can't adequately damage it, like Lanturn and Choice-locked Floatzel, or against Pokemon that it forces out, like Regirock and Gastrodon. It is also important to note that when not on a full rain team Ludicolo should be preserved for the late-game and rarely used early on, as it has an easier time sweeping once checks and counters are weakened. It can, however, be used as a late-game breaker if need be. If Ludicolo is up against a slower foe that is within range of a KO and isn't likely to switch out, it should usually just use an attack to revenge kill the opposing Pokemon so as not to take any damage. Lastly, Ludicolo should look for the opposing team to be generally weakened to begin its sweep, as while its good coverage lets it cover most of the metagame on its own, its middling power can compromise its sweeping chances.
On dedicated rain teams, rain setters like Liepard and Volbeat are important teammates for Ludicolo. Both of them also have access to U-turn, which allows them to safely bring Ludicolo into play. Other pivots, such as Alolan Raichu and Primeape, can also safely bring Ludicolo into battle. Slow pivots like Lanturn and Probopass are particularly useful for minimizing its chances of taking damage. Other Swift Swim users, such as Kabutops and Poliwrath, can fit onto rain teams with Ludicolo and appreciate its ability to break past their common checks, like Gastrodon. Entry hazard support from the likes of Golurk and Mudsdale can aid Ludicolo in punishing its switches and breaking past foes more easily in general. Powerful physical attackers like Stoutland, Gurdurr, and Zangoose adequately pressure the specially defensive Pokemon that Ludicolo struggles to break past, like Assault Vest Hitmonchan and Type: Null, while in return it can pressure the physically defensive Pokemon they're troubled with themselves, like Regirock.
Surf is an option for consistent and reliable damage over the less accurate Hydro Pump, though the loss in power is quite notable. Scald sacrifices power for better accuracy than Hydro Pump and a chance to burn that Surf doesn't have. However, given that Ludicolo looks to power through most foes, this often isn't a good option. Ludicolo can use Z-Crystals like Grassium Z and Icium Z to lure in and remove specific threats, but this cuts into the power its other attacks would have with a Life Orb, which is notably more valuable. Waterium Z is also a nice option due to its insane power in the rain, though it often isn't preferred for similar reasons. A Substitute + Leech Seed set can be used due to Ludicolo's decent defensive typing, though its poor physical bulk makes this hard to pull off.
Specially Bulky Pokemon: Various specially bulky Pokemon are capable of tanking Ludicolo's attacks easily due to its only decent Special Attack. Examples include Roselia and Type: Null.
Bulky Attackers: Due to Ludicolo's poor bulk overall, it is heavily pressured by strong offensive Pokemon that it fails to KO, including Assault Vest Hitmonchan.
Strong Priority: Strong priority attacks from Spiritomb and Skuntank can heavily dent Ludicolo and even revenge kill it after it's been whittled down some. Kangaskhan's priority attacks are particularly troublesome, as with Fake Out, it can damage Ludicolo while burning rain turns.
Abomasnow and Aurorus: By virtue of Snow Warning, Abomasnow and Aurorus can disrupt Ludicolo's rain. Abomasnow can tank any hit while pressuring Ludicolo with powerful STAB attacks, while Choice Scarf Aurorus can outspeed and OHKO Ludicolo with Freeze-Dry.

smogon_description:
Unlike its fierce competitors such as Bellsprout, Bulbasaur, and Deerling, Seedot lacks usable offensive stats, a secondary STAB, and even a decent Speed tier, with only Explosion to set it apart from other Chlorophyll attackers. Sun hyper offense teams are also exceedingly rare due to the lack of an auto-setter and the playstyle's rough matchup versus the majority of teams.
Seedot should try its best to blow holes into the opposing team after a teammate sets up Sunny Day. Seedot should also try to obtain a Growth boost although its frailty and inability to offensively pressure anything prevents it from reliably doing so. Other Chlorophyll sweepers such as the previously mentioned Bulbasaur and Bellsprout are much more capable than Seedot and outclass it in nearly every regard.

name: Shiftry
smogon_description:
Shiftry is an offensive force to be reckoned with as a result of its solid offensive typing, decent mixed attacking stats, and strong STAB options such as Knock Off, Leaf Storm, Seed Bomb, and Sucker Punch. Because of its mixed coverage, Shiftry manages to stand apart from other Dark- and Grass-types in the tier and is a massive threat to teams that are overly reliant on Pokemon such as Gurdurr, Mudsdale, and Regirock to check physical attackers. Shiftry becomes even more threatening under sun because of its ability Chlorophyll doubling its Speed, which allows it to also threaten opposing sun teams. It can also function well as an offensive user of Defog because its typing gives it the ability to threaten common entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale, Golurk and Regirock, allowing it to clear the field of entry hazards on the turn that they switch out. However, its great offensive typing curses it with weaknesses to common attack typings such as Fire, Flying, Poison, and Ice, and its poor bulk doesn't make matters much better. Although its Speed is far from terrible, Shiftry is outsped by common offensive Pokemon such as Primeape and Silvally-Fairy, and its main method of mitigating this in Sucker Punch isn't very reliable due to how it can be taken advantage of. Finally, as a purely physical wallbreaker, Shiftry faces competition from other Dark-types in the tier such as Absol and Alolan Raticate, both of which, while slower, are stronger.
Knock Off is one of Shiftry's two Dark-type STAB moves, and on top of hitting a lot of Pokemon that resist Leaf Storm fairly hard, it removes the opposing Pokemon's item. This effectively cripples Pokemon reliant on their Assault Vest or Eviolite to check Shiftry and its teammates, like Eelektross, Hitmonchan, and Ferroseed. Sucker Punch is the second of Shiftry's Dark-type STAB moves. It can be used to score KOs on faster but frailer Pokemon like Alolan Raichu or Floatzel after they take a bit of damage beforehand. Do keep in mind, however, that it fails if the foe doesn't attack, which can be taken advantage of by Pokemon with reliable recovery like Swanna. Leaf Storm is Shiftry's main Grass-type STAB attack, and it can be used to hit physically defensive Pokemon like Aggron and Mawile harder than its Dark-type moves, which neither of them mind all that much. Defog can be opted for if your team lacks hazard control, which is good for more offensive teams due to the pressure Shiftry puts on common hazard setters like Regirock. Alternatively, Low Kick hits Alolan Sandslash, which could otherwise take advantage of Shiftry. Explosion gives Shiftry access to a one-time physical attack with 250 Base Power at the cost of Shiftry itself. Explosion is Shiftry's best attack against Skuntank, which resists both of Shiftry's STAB types and threatens it with Poison Jab, and Explosion also has the secondary advantage of severely weakening even some of the most physically bulky non-Normal-resistant Pokemon in the tier, such as Gurdurr.
Special Attack investment isn't necessary, as even without it, Leaf Storm hits its main targets harder than any of the physical attacks do. A Lonely nature is used to increase Shiftry's attacking power without lowering its Special Attack. A Hasty nature can be used if you wish to outspeed certain neutral-natured Pokemon such as Kangaskhan and Stoutland, though this does cause Shiftry to lose out on certain KOs. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, making it even more threatening on and against sun-based teams. Life Orb strengthens all of Shiftry's attacks, but it comes with the downside of recoil damage.
Use Knock Off a lot early on, as it's Shiftry's most reliable STAB move and cripples defensive Pokemon like Tangela by removing Eviolite, rendering it unable to check Shiftry as effectively. If you're using Defog on Shiftry, bring it in on entry hazard setters that it threatens like Bronzor and Regirock, and Defog on the turn they switch. Sucker Punch is a great tool for revenge killing, but as mentioned before, it can be exploited by Pokemon that can recover their health or set up such as Swanna and Jynx. Exercise caution when using Explosion, as Shiftry only gets one use at the move, so refrain from using it until Shiftry is no longer required and wants to dish out one last heavy hit. Shiftry is easy to wear down due to Life Orb recoil, entry hazards, and its poor bulk, so not letting it take much or any unnecessary damage is smart, especially if it's the team's only form of entry hazard control.
Fire-types like Simisear and Turtonator break through bulkier Grass-types and physical walls like Tangela for Shiftry, while Shiftry provides entry hazard removal for them and combats the Ground-, Rock-, and Water-types that threaten them such as Carbink and Lanturn. Fighting-types like Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, and Primeape place pressure on both physical walls and opposing Dark-types for Shiftry, and it pressures Psychic-types in return. Pokemon that resist Fighting such as Musharna, Swanna, and Qwilfish synergize well defensively with Shiftry, as they handle the Fighting-types that force it out, especially those with Mach Punch like Gurdurr and Hitmonchan. They appreciate how Shiftry deals with Electric- and Psychic-types like Lanturn and Alolan Raichu. Slow users of Volt Switch like Eelektross and Lanturn work to get Shiftry in as safely as possible. Each has its own benefits: Eelektross beats Pokemon like Tangela, while Lanturn can cure Shiftry of status with Heal Bell and can check Fire-types. Entry hazard setters such as Qwilfish and Mudsdale pair well with Shiftry because hazards pressure Fire-types and faster but frailer Pokemon, which can't take Shiftry's moves as well if they are up, particularly Sucker Punch. Shiftry can even keep the entry hazards up with Explosion while either severely weakening the opposing Pokemon or securing a KO. If Shiftry's on a sun team, Sunny Day users like Liepard, Regirock, and Volbeat are definitely important. Fellow sun sweepers like Simisear and Victreebel pair well with it too. Victreebel can absorb Toxic Spikes for Shiftry, which helps it remain around for longer, and Shiftry can put holes in teams and make it easier for the other sun sweepers to finish them off.
Knock Off is Shiftry's main Dark-type STAB move that removes the item of the opposing Pokemon and hits a lot of Pokemon that resist Seed Bomb for neutral damage. Sucker Punch is Shiftry's secondary Dark-type STAB move, and it improves Shiftry's matchup against fast but frail Pokemon such as Alolan Raichu and Dodrio, especially after a Swords Dance. Low Kick is an option over Seed Bomb as it allows it to hit Aggron and Alolan Sandslash harder.
An Adamant nature helps to increase Shiftry's power and give it stronger priority, but a Jolly nature can be used to let it outspeed neutral-natured Pokemon like Adamant Skuntank. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, letting it outspeed the entire unboosted metagame as well as some Choice Scarf users like Primeape, which makes it threatening on and against sun teams. Life Orb gives all of Shiftry's moves a bit more power, at the cost of some of its health for every attack. Black Glasses is an alternative that doesn't deal recoil damage to Shiftry and still boosts the power of Knock Off and Sucker Punch, but it doesn't give Seed Bomb a boost in power.
Using Knock Off a lot early on to weaken checks and remove the items of checks is good for pressuring them and making them unable to keep Shiftry in check. Finding opportunities to set up a Swords Dance on Pokemon that Shiftry forces out like Bronzor, Gastrodon, or Sableye is ideal due to their passivity. Once Shiftry manages to use Swords Dance, it should weaken and break as much of the opposing team as it can, paving the way for its teammates to and clean up. Sucker Punch allows Shiftry to check faster but frailer Pokemon as well as setup sweepers. None of them appreciate taking a Sucker Punch, especially if Shiftry uses Swords Dance beforehand. Shiftry is really frail and doesn't like taking even resisted hits when it doesn't have to, so be sure to keep Shiftry as healthy as possible when attempting to set up.
This set has problems with physical walls due to a lack of mixed coverage, so good partners are Pokemon such as Simisear and Drampa that can severely weaken or KO physically defensive walls like Tangela and Alolan Persian. Primeape greatly appreciates Shiftry's ability to pressure Ghost-types like Sableye and Jellicent, and in return gives Shiftry set-up opportunities with U-turn. Similarly, Hitmonchan is able to check Ice- and Fire-types like Aurorus and Simisear for Shiftry, and can provide entry hazard removal to aid Shiftry in remaining alive for as long as it can. Skuntank resists both of Shiftry's STAB moves, so Ground- and Steel-types that can handle it like Mudsdale and Aggron are beneficial. Mudsdale in particular is notable because of its ability to check Fighting-types like Primeape, Hitmonchan and Gurdurr that Shiftry struggles with. Other Pokemon that check Fighting-types and can tank Fighting-type moves for Shiftry such as Silvally-Fairy, Musharna, Oricorio-G, and Swanna make for good partners, and Shiftry helps them in return by removing Eviolite from Pokemon such as Gurdurr, Type: Null and Ferroseed, making them easier to handle. Slower users of Volt Switch and U-turn such as Eelektross, Lanturn and Type: Null make for good partners due to their ability to get Shiftry in on some of the more passive Pokemon they tend to bait in, like Audino, opposing non-Ice Beam Lanturn, and Sableye, all of which Shiftry takes advantage of and sets up on. Shiftry likes entry hazards being up on the opposing side so that its moves are even harder to come in on, especially after a Swords Dance, so hazard setters like Metang and Qwilfish pair well with it. If Shiftry is being used on a sun team, Sunny Day users like Liepard, Regirock, and Volbeat alongside other sun sweepers are necessary. Sun sweepers like Victreebel and Leafeon benefit from Shiftry's presence because they are often able to weaken their shared checks, with one allowing the other to clean up as a result.
Knock Off is Shiftry's most reliable physical STAB attack, hits Pokemon like Jynx and Oricorio-G for super effective damage, and removes the items of the opposing Pokemon, which is good for crippling defensive Pokemon. Rock Slide hits Fire- and Flying-types like Simisear and Swanna for super effective damage. Low Kick allows it to hit Aggron and Alolan Sandslash harder than anything else. Alternatively, Explosion is used for taking a huge portion of health from Pokemon that Shiftry lures in, like Skuntank and Gurdurr, as well as for generating momentum. Defog can also be used as a means of emergency hazard control in order to have a better matchup versus entry hazard stacking teams.
Choice Scarf allows Shiftry to outspeed Pokemon like Jynx, Oricorio-G, and Swanna, even with an Adamant nature, which lets Shiftry hit as hard as possible. Chlorophyll doubles Shiftry's Speed under sun, making sure Shiftry outspeeds every opposing Chlorophyll user under it.
Using Knock Off a lot early on is smart, as it keeps opponents from immediately suspecting Shiftry's set. Refrain from using Rock Slide or otherwise making it obvious that you're using a Choice Scarf set until need be, as this will make the set ineffective at luring in faster threats. This set isn't very common in comparison to the other two, so take advantage of how it's unexpected by luring in the faster Pokemon that normally force Shiftry out like Simisear and Skuntank and KOing them. Shiftry serves as a solid revenge killer, as well, due to its lack of reliance on Sucker Punch for picking things off, so take advantage of Choice Scarf by taking down normally faster Pokemon like Alolan Raichu and Oricorio-G. Explosion still packs a punch despite the lack of a Life Orb boost, so use it to deal heavy damage to Pokemon like Skuntank and weakened physical walls.
Special wallbreakers like Aurorus, Drampa, and Haunter place pressure on Pokemon that Shiftry struggles with breaking, such as bulky Grass-resistant Pokemon like Tangela, Oricorio-G, and Mawile. In return, Shiftry cripples their switch-ins with Knock Off and can weaken them with Explosion, making them easier to KO. Fighting-types like Primeape appreciate Shiftry luring in and beating Flying-types and keeping out Ghost- and Psychic-types, and they beat the Dark-types that give it trouble like Alolan Raticate and Skuntank. Pokemon such as Silvally-Fairy and Musharna take on opposing Fighting-types such as Hitmonchan, while Shiftry's Explosion weakens or removes Dark- and Poison-types for them. Entry hazard setters like Ferroseed and Qwilfish make Shiftry's moves even harder to switch into, and Shiftry can keep the hazards up for longer by preventing Defog and Rapid Spin with Explosion. Qwilfish also acts as a Fighting-type check for Shiftry. Checks to Fire-types are important, as while Shiftry does outspeed them and possess good options for them, it prefers to have something to fall back on should it get locked into Leaf Blade, so Pokemon like Assault Vest Hitmonchan and Lanturn make for good partners. Checks to Ice-types are important for the same reason, so Shiftry appreciates Pokemon such as Lycanroc, Assault Vest Crabominable, and Alolan Sandslash. Shiftry also handles some of their collective weaknesses to typings like Ground, Psychic and Water. Pokemon that can easily bluff Choice Scarf sets such as Z-Lovely Kiss Jynx and Primeape pair well with Shiftry, preventing any suspicion in regard to Shiftry's set.
A purely specially offensive or specially biased mixed set is an option, and Shiftry even has access to Nasty Plot to boost the power of those moves. Solar Beam can be used over Leaf Storm on the mixed set if Shiftry is on a sun team so that Shiftry has a more spammable Grass-type STAB attack that doesn't drop its Special Attack; however, it's fairly useless outside of sun, and it's less strong than Leaf Storm. Pickpocket can be used on the Choice Scarf set to steal the opposing Pokemon's item if Shiftry loses its Choice Scarf, which can be useful for crippling defensive Pokemon in the event that Shiftry takes a Knock Off. A Lum Berry can be used on the Swords Dance sets to let Shiftry ignore a status condition once and have a slightly easier time setting up as a result. It's noticeably weaker without the boost from Black Glasses or a Life Orb, though. Synthesis gives Shiftry a form of reliable recovery, taking advantage of the switches it can force, but it usually prefers having a move to hit Alolan Sandslash or remove entry hazards as the final move on the mixed set, and it struggles to find room for Synthesis on any other set. Furthermore, Shiftry really doesn't need recovery, as its main priority should be breaking as much as it can. Grassium Z can be used on the Swords Dance set to turn Seed Bomb into Bloom Doom, which can be nice for luring Pokemon like Skuntank and taking them out after a Swords Dance boost. Normalium Z can be used on non-Choice Scarf sets with Explosion to still hit hard and not lose Shiftry in the process. It should be noted that Breakneck Blitz is slightly less strong than Explosion, and this takes away from the surprise factor that Explosion has. Flyinium Z can be used with Hurricane to lure and KO Gurdurr and Hitmonchan, and Shiftry can do this easier with Nasty Plot.
Poison-types: Muk and Skuntank can all deal heavy damage to Shiftry with their respective Poison-type STAB moves and don't mind Knock Off much, and Skuntank even resists both of Shiftry's STAB types. They do have to watch out for Explosion, however, boosted in power or not.
Fighting-types: Combusken, Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, and Primeape all resist Sucker Punch and force Shiftry out due to either outspeeding it or having Mach Punch; however, none of them except for Combusken and Hitmonchan want to be brought in on Leaf Storm, Gurdurr hates losing its Eviolite to Knock Off, and none of them wants to take an Explosion. Combusken can shield itself from Explosion and obtain a Speed boost with Protect, and it resists both of Shiftry's STAB types. Primeape can generate momentum for its team by using U-turn on the turn Shiftry switches.
Faster Pokemon: Pokemon such as Kangaskhan, Primeape, Rotom-F, and Pinsir all have the power to OHKO Shiftry due to its frailty. The Choice Scarf set does deal with almost all of them, though, and when facing other sets, they have to take a Sucker Punch before they get to attack Shiftry.
Priority: As a result of Shiftry's frailty, priority often leaves dents in it or KOs it with enough prior damage. Pokemon like Abomasnow, Gurdurr, Hitmonchan, Kangaskhan, and Zangoose all threaten Shiftry with either super effective or strong neutral priority moves.
